uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/faster-checkout-carts-synced-across-devices-via-shop; date: October 05, 2026; title: Faster checkout, carts synced across devices via Shop; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Shop]; text: Shop can now verify who a shopper is while they're browsing your store, even before they make a purchase. For Shop users, this means checkout loads faster, carts sync across devices, sign-in is sped up with one-tap, and the Buy with Shop Pay button is pre-filled for a smoother, higher-converting checkout. Browsing activity also syncs to a shopper's Shop account, so Shop can resurface items they viewed and abandoned carts, helping you close the loop on conversions. What this means for you: * Faster checkout *- less friction, faster load times * *Carts follow shoppers - carts sync and stay up to date across a shopper's devices * Better-converting Shop Pay button - personalized to show the card a shopper last used * One-tap sign-in - for Shop users signing into their customer accounts * Built-in recovery - Shop reminds shoppers to finish carts they left behind * Two-way sync - carts started in the Shop app carry over to your storefront, and vice versa Now supported on all browsers. Learn more in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/shop/customer-experience#shopping-activity-sync-with-shop-accounts]

Get started with right-to-left languages by adding them in your admin.; links: [text: in your admin; href: https://admin.shopify.com/settings/languages]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/schedule-and-test-discounts-with-rollouts; date: October 02, 2026; title: Schedule and test discounts with Rollouts; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now include discounts in Rollouts to run coordinated campaigns and test different offers before launching more broadly. Schedule discount changes: Launch a new offer to a portion of online store traffic, then expand when you're ready. Compare offers: Test discount changes against your existing offers and review conversion results to help decide which offer to keep. Launch changes together: Schedule a discount to go live alongside your theme and checkout changes in a single rollout. Your discount’s existing customer eligibility rules still apply. You can also continue using discount start and end dates to schedule standalone promotions. Learn more about discounts scheduling and testing in our help documentation.; links: [text: help documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/markets/rollouts]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/design-a-fully-bespoke-store-with-canvas; date: October 01, 2026; title: Design a fully bespoke store with Canvas; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Online Store]; text: Canvas is a new design surface for your online store. Every page is laid out together in one interactive, infinite workspace, so you can see how your whole store feels and work on any part of it in context. In Canvas, you can: * Pan across every page of your store and zoom in on any detail * Click any element to edit it directly, or tell Sidekick what you want in the chat * See Sidekick's changes land in real time, from a single section to a store-wide redesign * Preview the real, working store, with interactions, animations, and different products, collections, and screen sizes * Canvas is rolling out to existing stores over the coming days. Go to Online Store > Themes to create a new theme in Canvas, or duplicate a Shopify theme or custom theme in Canvas. Your original theme stays in the current theme editor. At launch, Canvas doesn't support third-party themes from the Shopify Theme Store, Markets, rollouts, translations, or app blocks and app embeds. Themes edited in Canvas don't receive theme updates. Learn more about designing your store in Canvas in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: designing your store in Canvas; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/online-store/themes/canvas]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/add-your-own-notes-to-shopify-analytics; date: October 01, 2026; title: Add your own notes to Shopify Analytics; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Your reports show what changed. You know why. Now, you're able to capture that story directly in Shopify Analytics. Add annotations to supported time-series reports for the moments that shape your business, like a campaign launch, creator mention, supplier change, promotion, or operational improvement. Instead of leaving that context in memory, spreadsheets, or team threads, it stays beside the data where you expect to see shifts. When you return to a report weeks or months later, you and your team can quickly understand why performance changed without piecing the story back together. From the annotations panel, you can: - Add a title, description, date or date range, and annotation type - Use our auto-detected annotation categories or choose your own - Edit, delete, and see who created each annotation - Search and filter context from your team, installed apps, and Shopify Annotations are shared with staff who have Reports permission and appear alongside context from Shopify and installed apps. Together, they create one shared history of what changed, what your business did, and why it mattered. Learn more about annotations here.; links: [text: here; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/reports-overview]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shop-is-now-at-shop-com; date: September 29, 2026; title: Shop is now at shop.com; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: Shop's web experience has moved from shop.app to shop.com. Your store, products, and channel settings are unaffected — the change only affects the web address shoppers use to reach Shop. What's changing Shop's web experience now lives at shop.com instead of shop.app Existing shop.app links redirect automatically to shop.com What you need to do Nothing. Your store, products, and channel settings carry over exactly as they are. If you've linked to shop.app anywhere (social bios, ads, etc.), you can update those links to shop.com at your convenience, though the redirect will continue to work.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/return-window-overrides-now-available; date: September 29, 2026; title: Return window overrides now available; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now set return window overrides by market for specific collections, products, or variants. Overrides let you choose a different return period than your default return window - for example, 14 days for seasonal items instead of your standard 90 days. How it works * Overrides replace the default return window: If an item matches an override, that override's return window gets applied instead of your default or market-specific window. * The shortest override wins: If an item matches more than one override, the shortest matching return window applies. * Final sale still wins: Items marked as final sale can't be returned (or cancelled), even if they also match a return window override. * Default rules apply otherwise: If an item isn’t final sale and doesn’t match an override, your market-specific return window applies. If no market-specific rules are set, your default return window applies. Where to set it Settings > Policies > Return and cancellation rules > Select specific market rules to modify > You can then select a target collection, product, variant to apply a return window override to. Example Set a 14‑day window for your “Holiday 2026” collection while keeping your storewide default at 90 days. Learn more in return window overrides.; links: [text: return window overrides; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders/returns/return-rules]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/local-delivery-orders-in-shopify-pos; date: September 28, 2026; title: Local delivery orders in Shopify POS; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [POS]; text: Staff can now create local delivery orders at checkout in Shopify POS. When a customer can't take an item home, you can arrange delivery in the same sale. You no longer need to ask them to reorder online or leave notes on the order. Local delivery uses the delivery zones and rates you already set up for your online store. When you add shipping to a cart and the customer's address is in one of your delivery zones, local delivery shows up with your other shipping rates. Select it, confirm the customer's phone number, add any delivery instructions, and check out. The delivery address and fee show in the cart, on the receipt, and on the customer-facing display. You can then prepare and fulfill the order in POS, the same way you handle local delivery orders from your online store. Things to know Staff permissions: Local delivery uses your existing POS permissions, with some updates to how they apply: * To create local delivery orders, staff need Create shipping and delivery orders (previously Ship to customer). * To fulfill local delivery orders, staff now need Fulfill shipping, pickup, and delivery orders (previously Fulfill shipping and pickup orders). Previously, staff could fulfill local delivery orders without this permission. * Review your staff roles before using local delivery in POS and add the fulfillment permission for anyone who needs to fulfill these orders. Fulfillment: * Every physical item in the order must be delivered. You can't mix local delivery with shipping or pickup in one order. * Gift cards and digital items can be added to a local delivery order. * Delivery must be within the same country as the location. Requirements: POS Pro, Shopify POS version 11.16 or later, and local delivery set up for the location in your Shopify admin. Learn more in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/order-management/local-delivery-orders]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/run-inventory-counts-in-pos; date: September 28, 2026; title: Run stock counts in POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: Shopify POS now lets store staff run cycle and full stock counts directly in POS, making it easier to count inventory on the sales floor while keeping planning, review, and approval in Shopify Admin. In Shopify Admin, users with the required permissions can create and schedule a stock count, select the location where the count will take place, and choose the products to include. Once created, the count automatically appears under Products > Stock counts in POS at the selected location. In Shopify POS, staff with the inventory permission can open the count and record what’s on hand by scanning barcodes or entering quantities manually. When the count is complete, it is submitted for review in Shopify Admin. Submitting a stock count from POS doesn’t immediately update inventory quantities. Users with the required permissions can review the completed count and any discrepancies before approving it and applying the resulting inventory adjustments. Shopify also keeps a record of what was counted, when the count was completed, and who performed it, providing an audit trail for inventory adjustments . Running stock counts in Shopify POS requires POS Pro and Shopify POS v11.16 or later. Learn more about running stock counts in Shopify Admin and POS. Learn more about running stock counts in Shopify Admin and POS.; links: [text: Learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/inventory-management/changing-inventory-quantities-pos#perform-a-stock-count]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/use-metaobject-fields-in-analytics-reports; date: September 28, 2026; title: Use metaobject fields in Analytics reports; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Analytics]; text: If you attach a metaobject to a product, variant, customer, or order through a metafield, those fields can now be used in Analytics. A designer country, a warranty term, or a loyalty tier can group and filter a report the same way a custom metafield can. Merchant-owned metaobjects are already enabled. You can turn a definition off if you don't want it in reports. What you can do - Open a report and pick fields under Metaobjects, then the resource, the definition, and the field. For example, Designer, then Country. - Filter to a single value, like a designer in Italy. - Use the same fields in the query editor. - Turn a definition on or off in Settings > Metafields and metaobjects. Open the metaobject and use Filter or group data in Analytics. What stays the same - Your metaobjects, and the metafields that point to them, are unchanged. - Custom metafields and category metafields stay in the picker, in their own groups. - Metaobjects created by an app stay off until you or the app turn Analytics on for that definition.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/category-metafields-are-now-available-in-analytics; date: September 28, 2026; title: Category metafields are now available in Analytics; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Until now, the color, material, fit, and other attributes you set when you categorize a product stayed on the product page. To see which materials or colors actually sell, you had to export. Those category metafields now show up in Analytics as dimensions and filters, next to your custom metafields. If you already categorized products, there's nothing to turn on. The attributes your products use are there. What you can do - Group a sales report by Color, Material, Fit, Fabric, Size, Activity, or any other category metafield on your products. - Filter a report to a specific value, like organic cotton or a particular color. - Use them in Reports, Explore, and the query editor. What stays the same - How you categorize products hasn't changed. - Custom metafields still work the way they do today. - If a product has more than one value for an attribute, Analytics keeps those values together on one row so sales aren't counted twice.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/tax-is-now-calculated-on-return-shipping-fees; date: September 25, 2026; title: Tax is now calculated on return shipping fees; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Orders]; text: Starting October 23, 2026, for merchants using Shopify Tax or Tax Platform in the United States, return shipping fees will be taxed like any other shipping charge. Your existing shipping tax settings still apply — if you’ve set shipping to be untaxed in a state, return shipping fees in that state remain untaxed. *What you need to do: * - If you use a manual workaround today to calculate, collect, import, or reconcile tax on return shipping fees, review it before October 23 to avoid double-counting tax. - Otherwise, no action is required. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-analytics-session-measurement-improvements; date: September 21, 2026; title: Shopify Analytics session measurement improvements; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Starting September 21, 2026, Shopify is improving the sessions experience in Analytics to give merchants a cleaner view of real shopper activity. As a result, sessions, conversion rate, and other session-based metrics might look different after this update. This doesn't necessarily mean that your traffic, orders, or customer behavior changed. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/multiple-barcodes-in-variants; date: September 08, 2026; title: Product variants now support multiple barcodes; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Products]; text: Until now, a product variant could hold one barcode. That's a problem when the same item arrives with a manufacturer's UPC on the box, your own private-label EAN on the shelf tag, and an ASIN on a marketplace listing. You had to pick one and keep the rest in a spreadsheet. Now you can add up to 20 barcodes to a variant, and any of them identifies the product. What you can do Add, scan, and remove barcodes right on the variant details page, or from the Shopify app on your phone. Give each barcode a type: UPC, EAN, ISBN, GTIN, or ASIN, and we'll check the value against that standard's format, so a mistyped digit gets caught as you enter it. You can also select Custom for internal codes that don't follow a standard. Update barcodes across many variants at once in the bulk editor. Import and export the full set using the Variant Barcodes column in your product CSV. Channels continue to read the first barcode provided. Scan and find variants on POS with multiple barcodes and SKU (changelog). What stays the same Your existing barcodes are already in place, so there's nothing to migrate. The first barcode on a variant is still the one used wherever a single barcode is expected, which means your labels, sales channel feeds, and apps keep working exactly as they do today.; links: [text: changelog; href: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/scan-and-search-variants-with-multiple-barcodes]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/scan-and-search-variants-with-multiple-barcodes; date: September 01, 2026; title: Scan and search variants with multiple barcodes; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Shopify POS can now identify a product variant using any barcode associated with it, making it easier for staff to find the right product when items have different barcodes across suppliers, channels, or packaging. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/check-connectivity-status-from-pos-home; date: September 01, 2026; title: Check connectivity status from POS Home; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: You can now check your device’s connectivity status directly from POS Home. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/inventory-reports-now-show-on-hand-quantity; date: August 14, 2026; title: Inventory reports now show on-hand quantity; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Starting October 1, 2026 Inventory analytics models now measure stock by on-hand quantity instead of available quantity. This better reflects real world information of your physical inventory. On-hand quantity includes all units physically at a location, including units committed to open orders and units currently unavailable. Available quantity includes only units that are available to sell. What to expect From October 1 onward, these reports reflect everything you actually hold, not just what's sellable, so reported inventory may be higher than before by the number of committed and unavailable units. When writing ShopifyQL, this change can be seen when you query "FROM inventory" or "FROM inventorybylocation". Any reports powered by these models will reflect this change including: Products by sell-through rate Products by days of inventory remaining Inventory adjustment changes Inventory sold daily by product ABC product analysis Month-end inventory value Inventory transfer orders and shipments Month-end inventory snapshot Your past data won't change. Reporting before September 1, 2026 still shows available quantity, so historical numbers and trends stay exactly as they were. Only September 1 and later use on-hand.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/recommended-changes-to-checkout-field-settings-are-now-available; date: August 13, 2026; title: Recommended changes to checkout field settings are now available; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Eligible stores can now get personalized recommendations for customer information settings from the Checkout settings page in Shopify admin. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/managed-markets-is-ending-delivered-duty-unpaid-ddu-support; date: August 11, 2026; title: Managed Markets is ending Delivered Duty Unpaid (DDU) support; tags: [text: Removed]; areas: [Admin]; text: On August 24, 2026, Shopify Managed Markets will stop supporting delivered duty unpaid (DDU) in every country and region where it supports delivered duty paid (DDP). uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/enhanced-printed-receipt-editor; date: August 11, 2026; title: Enhanced printed receipt editor; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: We've updated printed receipts in Shopify POS so you can manage sale, return, exchange, gift, and gift card receipts in one place. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/view-app-added-annotations-on-your-analytics-charts; date: July 29, 2026; title: View app-added annotations on your analytics charts; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Analytics]; text: You can now see more business context directly on your analytics charts with annotations. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/add-a-bank-account-for-every-payout-currency; date: July 27, 2026; title: Add a bank account for every payout currency in Shopify Payments; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Payments]; text: We've removed the 8-currency limit on bank accounts for multi-currency payouts in Shopify Payments. Now the rule is simply one bank account per supported payout currency, so you can be paid out in every currency your region and plan allow. If you have an international customer base, multi-currency payouts let you receive money in the currency your customers paid in, rather than converting it back to your domestic currency first. That means fewer currency conversions, less exposure to exchange rates, and balances that sit in the same currencies you already use to pay suppliers, staff, and taxes abroad. Multi-currency payouts are available on eligible plans and regions, and fees apply to payouts you receive in non-domestic currencies. Ready to set this up? uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/quick-nearby-device-login; date: July 27, 2026; title: Quick nearby device login; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: Adding or swapping a POS device used to mean typing credentials on the new device - usually right when your store is the busiest. No Bluetooth? Scan a QR code from a logged-in device instead. By default, new devices are signed in for today only, so devices don't stay logged in after the event. Merchants who want longer sessions can enable Forever in POS channel admin. To learn more about turning this feature on per shop, permission and settings, visit the Help Center.; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/getting-started/securing-your-pos-setup#nearby-device-login]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/cart-sharing-on-shopify-pos; date: July 27, 2026; title: Cart sharing on Shopify POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: We’ve released Cart sharing for Shopify POS. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/collections-now-support-multi-source-and-variants; date: July 16, 2026; title: Collections now support multi-source and variants; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: This release expands collection capabilities to help merchants run complex merchandising strategies without workarounds such as duplicate lists or third-party apps. Previously, collections were created only by automated conditions or hand-picked products. You can now build a collection from multiple sources, target specific variants, reuse other collections, and more. Highlights include: Multiple sources in one collection. Combine automated conditions, hand-picked products, exclusions, other collections, and sources from apps in a single collection. Variant-level collections. Build collections around specific variants, such as a size or color. Those variants appear on collection pages, in filters, and in supported sales channels, including Online Store and POS. *Collections as building blocks. *Add a collection as a source inside another, so parent collections stay in sync when source collections change. ** Reuse across your business. **Apply the same collection in supported workflows such as discounts and taxes, including variant-level collections. ** Redesigned collections admin UI:** Use a visual grid for drag-to-reorder and bulk moves, list view for detail, and control over the sort order customers see on the collection page. Sidekick support. Build and update collections with Sidekick on admin and mobile. There are no breaking changes for existing collections. Existing collections continue to work and are updated in the new admin experience automatically. You do not need to delete or recreate them. If your store uses third-party or custom apps that interact with collections, ask your developers to update to API version 2026-07 to support these new capabilities. See developer instructions. Read help docs for more information.; links: [text: help docs; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/collections]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-managed-markets-now-available-in-canada-and-the-uk; date: July 15, 2026; title: Shopify Managed Markets now available in Canada and the UK; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Selling internationally is one of the biggest growth levers for Canadian and UK merchants and one of the most complex. Managed Markets removes that complexity by making Global-e your merchant of record for international orders. Your customers experience a localized checkout optimized for clarity and conversion, and you fulfill orders the same way you handle them at home. No surprise fees or delays What you get Transparent product pricing without surprise fees at checkout or delivery: International buyers see duties-inclusive prices, pay in their local currency, and have no surprise fees at delivery (DDP). Built-in international tax compliance. Global-e registers, collects, and remits tax in the destination country on your behalf. Discounted DHL Express and FedEx labels. Buy and print directly from your Shopify admin alongside your domestic orders. Automatic tariff management. Managed Markets classifies your products and assigns Harmonized System codes for your products for smooth customs clearance & accurate duties calculations. Import tax and duty collection is guaranteed - you’ll never receive an adjustment. Daily payouts in your local currency. CAD for Canadian stores, GBP for UK stores, processed daily by Shopify Payments alongside domestic sales. Local payment methods with Shopify Payments Learn more about Managed Markets – including eligibility, pricing, and set-up – in the Help Center.; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/international/managed-markets]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/multiple-product-discounts-on-the-same-item; date: July 15, 2026; title: Multiple product discounts on the same item; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Discounts]; text: You can now combine multiple product discounts on the same item, so overlapping promotions apply together without cart conflicts or workarounds. When a customer adds winter boots to their cart, both discounts apply automatically. What you can do Combine multiple product discounts on the same item. Combine discount codes with automatic product discounts on the same item. How it works Tag your discounts to group them (for example: loyalty, seasonal, affiliate). Set which tagged discounts can combine. Discounts apply automatically at checkout, following your rules. Learn more; links: [text: Learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/discounts/discount-combinations#product-discounts-same-line-item]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/drive-international-conversion-with-automated-duties-inclusive-pricing-from-shopify-managed-markets; date: July 10, 2026; title: Drive international conversion with automated duties-inclusive pricing from Shopify Managed Markets; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [International]; text: Shopify Managed Markets merchants can now use a managed pricing strategy across supported international markets. Pricing will account for cross-border costs like guaranteed duties and import taxes, transaction fees, and currency conversion in product prices, so international buyers can see stable, transparent pricing throughout their journey with no surprise fees at checkout or delivery. When managed pricing is active, duties and import taxes are included in the buyer’s product price instead of being shown as a separate duty line at checkout. The duty and import tax amounts displayed to buyers are guaranteed at checkout, which means Shopify Managed Markets covers the difference if the amount charged by customs is different. Managed international pricing also helps keep your payout amounts consistent with domestic orders. Buyers pay for import taxes, duties, foreign exchange fees, and Managed Markets fees directly through the adapted price, and your payout is processed by Shopify Payments. You can review the localized price breakdown on the product detail page using the View as demo. After an order is placed, you can review the price breakdown in the order’s payment section to see how the international price was calculated. Learn more about international pricing for Shopify Managed Markets; links: [text: Learn more about international pricing for Shopify Managed Markets; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/managed-markets/adaptive-pricing]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-copy-and-paste-steps-in-your-workflows; date: July 10, 2026; title: Flow: Copy and paste steps in your workflows; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Apps]; text: Building workflows often means recreating steps you've already set up somewhere else. Now you can copy an existing step and paste it, instead of rebuilding it from scratch. Select an action or condition step and use Cmd/Ctrl+C to copy it, then Cmd/Ctrl+V to paste. Flow keeps the copied step's configuration field values and, for conditions, its logic—so a pasted step arrives ready to use with only minor edits. You can paste within the same workflow or into a different one. This makes it faster to reuse steps you've carefully configured, whether you're expanding a single workflow or standardizing steps across several. A few things to note for this first release: - You can copy and paste one action or condition step at a time (triggers and multi-select copy/paste aren't supported yet). - Steps that use a custom configuration page, such as Send Marketing Email, can't be copied. For more information about how it works, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/c/shopify-flow/304]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/cpsc-efiling-fields-now-available; date: July 10, 2026; title: CPSC eFiling fields now available to Managed Markets merchants; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [International]; text: Effective July 8, 2026, U.S. importers of certain products are required by the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to perform electronic filing (eFiling) via the Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) during the entry process. Previously, records only needed to be available for goods upon request; now, certificate data must be transmitted for every regulated transaction at the border. Merchants and their suppliers are responsible for completing the electronic filing with government agencies. New feature: CPSC eFiling fields that are now available in product disclosures, giving you a structured way to store product-level data needed to maintain compliance on certain U.S. imports. The new disclosure fields support the reference CPSC eFiling path. The inputs are shared with integrated fulfillment providers; they are not shown to buyers: Reference PGA Message Set fields for products with certificate data pre-loaded in the CPSC Product Registry, using Certifier ID, Product ID, and Version ID. For merchants leveraging Managed Markets to sell into the US, Global-e will use these inputs for smoother, faster US Customs crossings. Merchants not using Managed Markets should consult CPSC resources and your broker, carrier, manufacturer, testing lab, or compliance advisor for best practices. Learn more about CPSC eFiling requirements and product disclosure setup in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: CPSC resources; href: https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling | text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/international/cpsc]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/define-and-manage-metafields-on-inventory-transfers; date: June 30, 2026; title: Define and manage metafields on inventory transfers; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Inventory]; text: Inventory transfers now support custom metafields in the Shopify admin and Admin GraphQL API. Use cases Transfer metafields are useful when your receiving, logistics, or inventory processes rely on data that the standard transfer fields don't cover: Lot, serial, and RFID tracking — attach lot numbers, serial numbers, or RFID identifiers to reconcile received units against what was shipped Logistics and customs details — store freight account numbers, bill of lading numbers, container references, incoterms, or customs-broker notes on inbound shipments ERP and WMS sync — let inventory apps attach reference numbers and mapping keys to keep transfers in sync with an external warehouse or ERP system Stocky migration — if you moved off Stocky, transfer metafields replace the supplier references, internal codes, lot codes, and approval notes you stored on Stocky transfers Duplicating transfers Metafields copy to the new transfer when you duplicate. Analytics Enable the Filter or group data in Analytics option on a transfer metafield definition to use it as a dimension or filter in Shopify Analytics.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-3-eu-import-customs-duty-arrives-july-1; date: June 26, 2026; title: Shopify now supports €3 EU import customs duty collection; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [International]; text: Shopify Managed Markets and Shopify's import tax and duty calculation now support the EU's flat €3 customs duty per tariff line on qualifying orders up to €150 shipped into the EU from outside the EU, effective July 1, 2026. If you use either product, Shopify handles this fee for you automatically. No settings changes required. What’s now supported In Shopify Managed Markets: The €3 fee is calculated, displayed, and collected at checkout. As your merchant of record, Global-e remits the duty to the destination country. Duty amounts shown at checkout are guaranteed, so neither you nor your customer pays more later. In Shopify import tax and duty calculation: The €3 fee is included in the duty amount calculated and displayed at checkout, so you can collect it from your customer alongside other duties. In both cases, the fee is charged in addition to VAT and any national handling fees, consistent with the EU regulation. What changed and who it affects The EU ended the €150 duty-free threshold for low-value imports and replaced it with a flat €3 customs duty per tariff line on qualifying orders up to €150 shipped into the EU from outside the EU. Customs counts the unique tariff classification lines in each parcel and applies €3 per line: A parcel of only apparel: €3 A parcel of apparel, cosmetics, shoes, and jewelry: €12 This affects you if you ship to EU customers from outside the EU, including from the UK. It does not affect intra-EU shipments. Learn more about these changes in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/taxes/eu/eu-tax-migrate]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/purchase-orders-now-create-transfers-to-move-inventory; date: June 22, 2026; title: Purchase orders now create transfers to move inventory; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: Purchase orders record what you ordered from a supplier and what it cost. Linked records - Each transfer stays linked to its purchase order, so what was ordered, what arrived and what it cost, are all connected. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/staff-attribution-improvements-in-pos; date: June 22, 2026; title: Staff attribution improvements in POS; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: We’re improving staff attribution over the next two updates, so it’s easier to credit the right team member for every sale. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/customer-accounts-get-a-design-uplift; date: June 17, 2026; title: Customer accounts get a design uplift; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Customer accounts]; text: Customer account pages get a design uplift that makes it easier for your customers to navigate their account, track orders, and take actions. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/unified-pos-staff-management; date: June 11, 2026; title: Unified staff permissions for retail teams; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Staff management for your entire team—POS and admin users—is now unified in Settings > Users. We’ve also made it easier to manage seasonal staff, high trust permissions and permissions across Shopify Plus organizations. Your existing users, permissions, and roles have been automatically migrated, so everyone keeps their current access. What’s new: Manage POS users in admin settings Set up POS users, assign roles, and manage PINs in Settings > Users instead of the POS channel. Assign organization level roles Shopify Plus merchants can now grant POS staff access across multiple shops within their organization with a single user profile—no duplicates needed. Suspend and reactivate seasonal staff Suspend or deactivate seasonal staff without deleting their accounts. When they return, reactivate them and keep their history. Assign multiple roles Create custom roles with the permission sets that make sense for your business. Give staff members as many roles as they need—like Store Manager and Marketer. New high-trust roles We’ve created new POS roles to make it easier to identify users with high-trust access. All users have retained their previous permissions, with one exception: POS Administrator (formerly “Full permissions”) POS Device Setup (for setting up new devices) POS User Administrator (for managing users) Organization POS Administrator (for creating, editing and deleting roles across all stores) Note: The ability to create, edit, or delete roles is now an organization-wide permission, not a shop-level one. For security, we haven’t automatically granted this broader access. If someone on your team previously managed roles for a single shop, you’ll need to assign them the Organization POS Administrator role if you want them to manage roles across all stores. Assigning existing roles to users is still possible with the POS User Administrator role, which has been assigned to anyone who had that permission previously. You may need to review and clean up your user and role lists as a result of this change. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/unlink-a-customer-from-your-custom-identity-provider; date: June 11, 2026; title: Unlink a customer from your custom identity provider; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Customer accounts]; text: If your store uses a connected OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider for customer accounts (such as Okta, Auth0, Microsoft Entra ID), you can now unlink a customer from your identity provider directly in the Shopify admin. When a customer's account is linked to the wrong subject in your identity provider, the customer might see the following error when they try to sign in: "The sign-in method you used doesn't match this account." Previously, fixing this required contacting Shopify Support. Now you can resolve it yourself. To unlink a customer: 1. From your Shopify admin, go to Customers. 2. Click the customer that you want to unlink. 3. In the customer details section, click Unlink next to your identity provider's ID, such as Okta ID or Auth0 ID. 4. Review the subject ID displayed in the confirmation dialog and compare it with the subject ID for this customer in your identity provider, if you have access to that information. If the subject IDs do not match, unlinking the customer should resolve the The sign-in method you used doesn't match this account. error. 5. Click Unlink to confirm. After you unlink, the customer is signed out. They can sign back in with their existing credentials, and a new link is created on their next sign-in. The customer's orders, and other store data aren't affected. This feature is available to stores on the Shopify Plus plan that have connected their own identity provider to customer accounts. Learn more: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/customers/customer-accounts/sign-in-options/identity-provider/connect#unlink-customer

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/schedule-publish-and-a-b-test-new-themes-and-checkout-and-customer-account-configurations; date: June 05, 2026; title: Schedule, publish, and A/B test new themes and checkout and customer account configurations; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: Rollouts now supports scheduling, gradually publishing and A/B testing your themes and checkout and customer accounts configurations. You can now: 1. Schedule an entire new checkout or theme to go live at a specific date and time. For example, switch from Dawn to Horizon on a specific date. 2. Temporarily swap to a different theme or checkout setup. For example, activating a BFCM theme for one week with automatic revert. 3. Gradually roll out a new theme or checkout configuration to a percentage of your visitors. For example, rolling out a new branding experience for your customer account pages. 4. Run an A/B test between two entirely different themes or checkout setups to find the winner. For example, A/B testing a new upsell block for your checkout page. 5. Schedule or test localized content per market. For example, test different CTA text for each region to see impact on conversions. In addition, a copy of your published theme or config is automatically created so you can continue to edit your live theme/checkout independently from your experiment. And with mutually exclusive experiments, you can run multiple live experiments at the same time. To get started, go to Markets > Rollouts in your Shopify admin and create a Rollout. Learn more about Rollouts in our help documentation.; links: [text: help documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/markets-new/rollouts]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/scatter-plots-and-radar-charts-are-now-in-shopify-analytics; date: June 04, 2026; title: Scatter plots and radar charts are now in Shopify Analytics; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: Custom reports in Shopify Analytics now support two new chart types: scatter plots and radar charts. These give you more ways to spot patterns and compare performance across your store data without exporting to a spreadsheet. Use scatter plots to see how two metrics relate. Plot revenue against units sold per product to find which products move volume but not margin. Plot session count against conversion rate per traffic source to see which channels actually convert, not just bring traffic. Each data point shows up as a dot, so clusters and outliers are easy to spot. Use radar charts to compare across multiple metrics at once. Look at product categories side by side across average order value, conversion rate, and return rate on one shared axis. The shape that emerges shows the relative strengths and weaknesses of each category at a glance, instead of bouncing between separate line or bar charts. Both chart types are available now in the visualization picker when you create or edit an existing report with compatible data. Learn more about chart types in custom reports in the Shopify Help Center.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-tax-has-expanded-to-canada; date: May 13, 2026; title: Shopify Tax has expanded to Canada; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Managing Canadian sales tax is complicated, which is why we're committed to making it better. Shopify Tax is bringing brand new features to your admin that will make it easier to collect the right amounts at the right time, and know where your business is liable. New Enhanced calculations Stay confidently compliant selling across Canada knowing that Shopify Tax is accurately calculating sales tax rates (GST, HST, PST, QST, and RST) based on your customer's province and showing each of those rates individually to your buyers. Smart categorization Is a single donut a snack, or breakfast? Five donuts? Six? In Canada, six or more donuts is zero-rated as a basic grocery; five or fewer is taxable as a snack food. We may never settle the philosophical question, but at Shopify, we can help you categorize your donuts (and everything else) for tax purposes. Shopify suggests the relevant category for your products and automatically applies the right rate based on Canadian rules. Furthermore, taxes assessed on shipping will now follow the rate on each individual good, ensuring that zero rated goods or orders with mixed tax rates are accurately taxed. Tax liability insights per province Tax liability insights are no longer just at the country level. Now, you’ll be able to track where you may have tax obligations across each province and territory. Liability insights analyzes your store's sales and compares it to government requirements to let you know where and how you may be required to register and collect. Learn more Shopify Tax in Canada is currently being released to Shopify stores that sell in and to Canada. New stores can start using it immediately, and existing stores will be notified by email as the product becomes available. Additional features soon to come. Learn more about these new features in the Help Center.; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/taxes/shopify-tax/shopify-tax-canada]

Try it now in the checkout and accounts editor to get your brand looking right across checkout, customer accounts, and sign-in.; links: [text: Checkout and Accounts Configuration API; href: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/mutations/checkoutAndAccountsConfigurationUpdate | text: checkout and accounts editor; href: https://admin.shopify.com/admin/settings/checkout/editor]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/simpler-inventory-transfers; date: May 11, 2026; title: Simpler inventory transfers; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: We redesigned the inventory transfer workflow to match how merchants actually move inventory. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/print-packing-slips-for-inventory-transfers; date: May 11, 2026; title: Print packing slips for inventory transfers; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Previously, staff fulfilling outgoing inventory transfers in Shopify POS had no way to print a packing slip to include with the shipment. Now, staff on POS Pro can generate and print a packing slip directly from the shipment details for any outgoing transfer. The slip uses the same familiar format as order packing slips, adapted for transfers — it lists the items being sent (variant name and quantity), the origin and destination locations, and transfer details like the reference name, date, notes, and tags. This gives staff and receiving locations a simple manifest to reference during handoff, helping reduce confusion about what was sent and what should arrive when moving inventory across stores, state lines, or borders.
