uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/sell-gift-cards-in-your-customers-local-currency; date: May 11, 2026; title: Sell gift cards in your customers' local currency; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: Merchants selling to multiple markets from a single shop can now sell and issue gift cards in any currency they operate it, not just the shop's primary currency. A USD-based store can issue EUR, CAD, GBP, or any other market currency gift card, with the value held in that currency end-to-end. This removes a long-standing blocker for merchants expanding internationally and for retail merchants in particular: a 10 USD gift card no longer shows up as 14.07 CAD at checkout for a Canadian buyer, and balances stay stable regardless of exchange rate movement between purchase and redemption. When creating a local currency gift card, you can choose how it can be redeemed: Redeemable only in its issued currency - the buyer experience and balance stay fixed, with no FX exposure. Redeemable in any store currency - the gift card can be used at any of your markets, with conversion applied at the time of redemption using the current exchange rate. This setting is selected at creation and can't be changed afterward. To get started, create a gift card product priced in a market currency and publish it to that market's catalog, or issue a gift card directly from the Gift cards section of your admin. Learn more about local currency gift cards; links: [text: Learn more about local currency gift cards; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/pricing/gift-cards#local-currency-gift-cards]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-new-action-to-get-analytics-data-using-shopifyql; date: May 09, 2026; title: Flow: New action to get analytics data using ShopifyQL; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Apps]; text: Using the new "Get analytics data" action, you can now use ShopifyQL inside your workflows to pull data from Shopify analytics (sales figures, sessions, inventory levels) and act on what you find. Query results become variables you can use in subsequent conditions and actions. Some examples of what you can do: * Schedule a report that includes your analytics data to go to Slack * Send an alert when sales drop below a certain threshold * Tag products when they hit a certain sales milestone * Get notified when sessions drop or increase on your storefront For more information, including limitations, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/get-analytics-data | text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/c/shopify-flow/304]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/collect-marketing-consent-on-the-account-component; date: May 08, 2026; title: Collect marketing consent on the account component; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Customer accounts]; text: The account component on your storefront now includes a marketing opt-in checkbox below the email field. Customers who select it are added to your email marketing subscriber list when they complete signing in. The checkbox uses the same email marketing opt-in setting for checkout and sign-in. To enable or change it, go to Settings > Checkout > Marketing opt-in in your admin. To learn more, refer to Adding an account component menu to your online store and Collecting customer contact information.; links: [text: Adding an account component menu to your online store; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/customers/customer-accounts/customize-customer-accounts/account-component | text: Collecting customer contact information; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/customer-contact-information]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/benchmark-comparisons-in-analytics-will-be-removed-on-may-19th; date: May 07, 2026; title: Benchmark Comparisons in Analytics will be removed on May 19th; tags: [text: Removed]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Benchmark Comparison data in Shopify Analytics will no longer show new data, and the feature will be fully removed on May 19, 2026. Alternatives: Use Metric Targets to set and track your own performance targets directly in your reports, or ask Sidekick for personalized guidance on your store's performance.; links: [text: Metric Targets; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/targets]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/product-variant-publishing; date: May 07, 2026; title: Product Variant Publishing; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: We've just released variant-level publishing for sales channels and catalogs. This helps merchants control exactly which product variants are visible to buyers in each channel or catalog without having to delete variants or create duplicate products. You can now unpublish individual variants from the product details page, the variant details page, or the bulk editor — keeping the variant and its history in your admin while hiding it from storefronts on the channels you choose. Use it to stage upcoming variants before launch by creating new variants in the unpublished state. Retire discontinued options, restrict region-specific variants like plug types to the right markets, offer bulk-quantity variants only to B2B customers, or keep limited-edition variants exclusive to your online store. Learn more about variant publishing; links: [text: Learn more about variant publishing; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/variants/publish-variants]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/assign-discounts-to-specific-markets; date: May 07, 2026; title: Assign discounts to specific markets; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: Assign discounts to specific markets and control exactly where they apply. Run an online-only flash sale without it hitting your retail locations. Create a wholesale offer that only reaches your B2B buyers. No workarounds needed. What's new: - Eligibility selector on the Discount Details page: Assign any code-based or automatic discount to one or more markets - Market and customer filters on the discounts list: Filter by market, customer segment, or specific customers to find what's active where - Discounts on the Market Details page: See all discounts assigned to a market at a glance. Preview how discounts resolve in context with the View-As mode in Markets graph view. Discounts by Market is available for all merchants on Basic plans and above who are on the new version of Markets. Learn more in our help documentation.; links: [text: help documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/discounts/managing-discounts#eligibility]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/inventory-adjustment-workflow-now-with-full-change-tracking; date: May 07, 2026; title: Inventory adjustment workflow now with full change tracking; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: When you adjust inventory in your admin, you’ll now see two modes in the popover: "Set To" - Enter your quantity. Shopify tracks the change automatically. "Adjust By" - Pick a source and destination for full movement tracking. Every adjustment, regardless of mode, now records the source, destination, who made the change, and when. You can view your full adjustment history any time. The Bulk Editor is unchanged and you can keep using it to set available quantities directly, no source or destination required. To learn more about these changes in detail, visit our help documentation.; links: [text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/products/inventory/adjusting-inventory/adjusting-inventory-quantities]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/annotations-bring-store-event-context-directly-to-your-analytics; date: May 05, 2026; title: Annotations bring store event context directly to your analytics; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Analytics]; text: We now visually display annotations with color-coded markers that show when store events happened alongside your data. Say your conversion rate drops on a Tuesday. Instead of wondering what happened, you hover over an annotation marker and see that a new theme was published that same day. Click it to open the annotation panel, which shows a full daily breakdown with every product published, every app installed, every event that might explain what you're seeing. To get started, open any report, turn on Show annotations in the Visualization panel, and markers appear on your chart immediately. You can filter down to specific event types like just product publishes or just system events from the annotation panel. Use the arrow buttons to navigate between days and spot patterns across time. Annotations cover three categories today: - Product events (published, unpublished) - Store changes (theme published, app installed, app uninstalled) - System events (data delays, metric definition changes). Product annotations are ranked by revenue, so your highest-impact events always surface first. Annotations are generated from your store activity which means no setup & nothing to configure. Learn more about analytics annotations; links: [text: Learn more about analytics annotations; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/custom-reports/annotations]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-see-exactly-what-changed-in-any-workflow-and-roll-it-back; date: May 05, 2026; title: Flow: View who edited, activated, or deactivated a workflow version; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Apps]; text: Every workflow now keeps a version history — edits, activations, and deactivations are logged with the staff member and timestamp. When something breaks, open version history from the workflow detail page to see who changed the workflow and when. Version history is available on all workflows. Any staff member with access to the Flow app can view the history and browse past versions. For more information, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/shopify-flow/manage/version-history | text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/apply-discounts-to-items-on-the-refund-page; date: May 04, 2026; title: Apply discounts to items on the refund page; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: What changed When issuing a refund from the refund page, you can now add, update, or remove a discount on eligible items without leaving the refund page. How it works 1. Open an order and navigate to the refund page. 2. Add, update, or remove a discount on any eligible item. 3. The page updates with the revised outstanding balance. 4. Issue the refund against the discounted amount. Why it matters Previously, applying a discount before issuing a refund required merchants to navigate to the order editing page first — adding unnecessary steps. Now merchants can apply the discount directly from the refund page. Applying a discount ensures your sales and tax reporting is accurate when issuing a refund.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/mark-fulfillments-without-tracking-as-delivered; date: May 03, 2026; title: Mark fulfillments without tracking as delivered; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: Mark as Delivered allows shipping fulfillments without carrier tracking in the Shopify admin to be marked as delivered. This allows merchants who ship with unsupported carriers to keep order delivery status accurate. Mark as delivered lets staff mark a shipping fulfillment as delivered from an order's Fulfilled card, or update multiple orders at once from the Orders page.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/manage-inventory-at-locations-without-activating-them-for-fulfillment; date: May 01, 2026; title: Track inventory that isn't for sale or fulfillment; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Inventory]; text: You can now view and update on-hand inventory at any active location. New: For variants that don’t fulfill orders from that location: - On-hand inventory is now shown and can be updated. - Any existing committed or unavailable quantities remain visible until they’re reduced to zero. - Available quantity won’t be shown, because the location isn’t used to fulfill new orders: - On the Inventory page, this is shown as "—" with a warning that "Location doesn't fulfill this variant" - On the Product variant page, this is shown as blank, with a warning, on the Location, that "Location doesn't fulfill this variant" Changed: On-hand inventory at these locations still won't be used to fulfill new orders, but can continue to be used for fulfilling existing committed orders.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-new-triggers-for-inventory-transfers-completed-and-inventory-transfer-ready-to-ship; date: April 30, 2026; title: Flow: New triggers for inventory transfer completed and inventory transfer ready to ship; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Apps]; text: Flow now has new triggers that start workflows when inventory transfers change status. Inventory transfers represent stock moving between your business locations — like sending products from a warehouse to a retail store. The Inventory transfer ready to ship trigger starts a workflow when a transfer has been prepared and is marked "ready to ship". Use this to build workflows that alert the receiving location, update logistics dashboards, and more. The Inventory transfer completed trigger starts a workflow when a transfer is fully received at its destination (either accepted or rejected). Use this to build workflows that update internal records, notify teams that stock has arrived, or kick off follow-up tasks like shelf stocking or inventory reconciliation. For more information, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify Flow community.; links: [text: Inventory transfer ready to ship; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/shopify-flow/reference/triggers/inventory-transfer-ready-to-ship | text: Inventory transfer completed; href: http://help.shopify.com/manual/shopify-flow/reference/triggers/inventory-transfer-complete | text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/shopify-flow/reference/triggers | text: Shopify Flow community; href: https://community.shopify.dev/c/shopify-flow/21]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/manage-all-your-pos-settings-in-one-place-with-the-new-pos-editor; date: April 30, 2026; title: Manage all your POS settings in one place with the new POS Editor; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: No more hopping between settings pages. The new POS Editor brings payments, receipts, tips, customer info, and apps into a single, familiar editor with a cleaner layout and faster navigation. What's changing: - One editor, one navigation. Payments, offline payments, local payment methods, app extensions, customer info, and receipt settings now live alongside Smart grid, Lock screen, Customer display, and Receipts - all in the POS Editor. - Cleaner payments experience. Turn a payment method on or off with a visibility toggle right where you're designing the checkout. Shop Pay, Tap to Pay, and local payment methods display their setup status inline; entity-level settings deep-link to the right admin surface. - Global settings, surfaced. Staff attribution, required checkout information, and customer receipt selection are grouped under a Global settings section for faster access. - Updated app management. Enabling an app in the editor now activates its POS block and action extensions in one step - no second trip to settings. - New split-panel navigation. The editor uses the same layout as the Online Store editor, so changes you make in a sub-panel stay in context with what you're previewing. What you need to do: Nothing! The updated editor rolls out automatically over the coming weeks. Existing permissions still apply. Staff who can manage payment providers or POS settings today will see the new editor with the same access. Learn more about customizing your POS with the POS Editor in the Help Center.; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/customize-pos/pos-editor]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-balance-domestic-wire-transfers; date: April 29, 2026; title: Shopify Balance Domestic Wire Transfers; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Balance]; text: We've added the capability for US merchants to initiate domestic wire transfers using Shopify Balance. This improvement allows business owners to manage their payments more efficiently and securely. Merchants can now send US domestic wire transfers to pay thier suppliers, contractors, vendors etc. Learn more about enabling US domestic wire transfers in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/finance/shopify-balance/managing-account/transfers]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/data-driven-insights-now-appear-on-your-analytics-dashboard; date: April 28, 2026; title: Data-driven insights now appear on your analytics dashboard; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Your analytics dashboard now shows a stream of insights at the top of the page, highlighting the most important trends in your business. Shopify's analytics insights are run daily, analyzing your sales, sessions, and fulfillment data across products, regions, channels, customer types, and more. We surface the top 5 findings ranked by business impact so that when you open your dashboard, you immediately see what's changed. Each insight comes with a status badge (Trending Up, Trending Down, or Top Performers). Click "See why" to open the full report & Sidekick launches alongside it with the insight pre-loaded so you can ask follow-up questions like "What should I do next?" For example, you might see that sales from returning customers have been trending up for 8 consecutive weeks, a signal to double down on your loyalty campaigns. Or that a specific region just became your top performer by sales, something you'd never have spotted on your own. Learn more about analytics insights; links: [text: Learn more about analytics insights; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/overview-dashboard#insights]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/set-and-track-targets-in-shopify-analytics; date: April 27, 2026; title: Set and track targets in Shopify Analytics; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Analytics]; text: You can now set targets for key metrics directly in Shopify Analytics. Pick a metric from gross sales, orders, conversion rate, or dozens more, add a filter like a specific sales channel or product, set a time period, the amount you plan to reach and you've got a target! A visual gauge tracks your progress in real time, showing percentage complete, current vs target value, and days remaining. For example, say you want to hit $20,000 in Net sales from your Online Store this quarter. Create a target, filter it to the Online Store channel, set Q2 as your time period, and the gauge instantly shows where you stand. Add it to your dashboard with one click and you'll see it every time you open Analytics. When you're managing multiple goals, the new Target index gives you a single view of everything you're tracking. Targets are designed to grow with your business. Set them for the week ahead, the month, the quarter, or a custom range up to two years out. Edit them anytime, even after the period ends. Create your first target today! Learn more about targets; links: [text: Target index; href: https://admin.shopify.com/analytics/targets | text: first target; href: https://admin.shopify.com/analytics/targets/new | text: Learn more about targets; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/targets]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/returns-and-exchanges-in-cart-for-pos; date: April 27, 2026; title: Returns and exchanges in cart for POS; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Returns, refunds, and exchanges now happen directly in the cart in Shopify POS v11.5. Instead of moving through separate workflows, staff can now complete these transactions in one place. This updated experience makes it faster and simpler to process returns and exchanges at the counter, while supporting a wider range of return and exchange scenarios. This update extends existing operational controls to the new in-cart workflow, including support for return reasons, Smart Grid and full cart functionality, refund handling, and staff permissions for return and exchange actions. We’ve also introduced new Return permissions in POS, including Manage item restock, Remove unfulfilled items, and Complete in-progress returns, which are all allowed by default at launch. The Require return reasons setting is also available and is turned off by default at launch. Review these permissions and settings to make sure they’re configured the way you want for your staff. If your Return & exchange orders manager approval setting was already enabled, it now applies to Manage item restock and Complete in-progress returns. Manager approval for Remove unfulfilled items is enabled by default. Watch the walkthrough and learn more in the Help Center documentation: Processing returns and refunds using Shopify POS and Exchanging an order on Shopify POS.; links: [text: Watch the walkthrough; href: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kN4OAaUpprg | text: Processing returns and refunds using Shopify POS; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/order-management/complete-refund-orders | text: Exchanging an order on Shopify POS; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/order-management/exchange]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/mid-session-cash-counts; date: April 27, 2026; title: Mid-session cash counts; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Previously, you could only count the cash in your register when opening or closing a session. Now, staff can perform a cash count at any point during an active shift. Simply tap the Register icon and select Count cash to verify the amount in your drawer whenever needed—whether you're doing a till check during a busy day, handing off to a new staff member mid-shift, or reconciling after a large cash deposit or removal. The count is automatically logged to your register session, helping you catch discrepancies early and maintain tighter control over your cash flow throughout the day. Learn more about the mid-session cash counts in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/cash-register-management]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/custom-discount-amounts-on-line-items-in-pos-now-apply-per-item; date: April 27, 2026; title: Custom discount amounts on line items in POS now apply per item; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [POS]; text: What's changing Starting with version 11.5, when you apply a fixed-amount custom discount to a line item in Shopify POS, the value you enter is now the discount per item instead of a total amount spread across the line. For example, on a line with 3 sweaters, entering a $5 fixed-amount discount used to take $5 off the whole line ($1.67 off each sweater). Starting in POS v11.5, that same $5 takes $5 off each sweater, for a $15 total discount. This matches how custom discounts already work in the Shopify admin and on Draft orders, and makes per-item pricing easier to explain to customers at the counter. View walkthrough What you'll see in POS - The amount field on the Add custom discount screen is now labeled Amount per unit with helper text confirming the discount applies to each item on the line. - The line item still shows the total discount applied (amount × quantity), so the cart total is clear at a glance. - Receipts continue to break out discounts the same way they do today. - Percentage discounts and discount codes are unchanged. If your store uses a third-party POS app that applies fixed-amount discounts (for example, a wholesale or loyalty app), the app will continue to work as it does today. The app developer may release an update later that takes advantage of the new per-item allocation; if you notice a change in how a particular app's discounts apply after that update, contact the app's support team. Learn more in the Help Center. Action required for developers in 2026-07 On API version 2026-07 and later: If your extension calls setLineItemDiscount or bulkSetLineItemDiscounts with FixedAmount, update the values you pass so they represent the per-unit discount.; links: [text: View walkthrough; href: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ONIBwRqgeNY | text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/discount-management/applying-discounts#line-item-custom-discounts]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/find-products-faster-in-shopify-pos-with-inline-search-suggestions; date: April 27, 2026; title: Find products faster in Shopify POS with inline search suggestions; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Searching for products in Shopify POS just got faster. Starting with POS v11.5, inline suggestions help retail staff complete searches with fewer keystrokes. As you type in the product search field, the next word completes inline as ghost text drawn from your local catalog. Press Space or Tab to accept the suggestion and jump straight to the product, no need to finish typing the word. Product search is one of the most frequent actions on the POS. For retailers with large catalogs, faster search means shorter queues, fewer abandoned lookups, and more time at the counter spent with customers instead of on the keyboard. Availabile for both iOS and Android in version 11.5

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/keyboard-shortcuts-and-navigation-in-shopify-pos; date: April 27, 2026; title: Keyboard shortcuts and navigation in Shopify POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: We've added keyboard navigation to Shopify POS so cart-building no longer requires switching between keyboard and touch. Retail staff on iPad and Android tablets with a hardware keyboard can now: - Open search with CMD+K and see all available shortcuts by holding CMD - Navigate Products, Orders, and Customers lists with arrow keys - Select a cart item or list result with Enter, or jump to one of the first nine with CMD+1–CMD+9 - Start checkout with CMD+Enter and exit flows with Escape This removes friction during the most type-heavy moments like product search, customer lookup, and checkout and establishes a consistent keyboard interaction model that Shopify and partner teams can extend across POS. Learn more about keyboard shortcuts the Shopify Help Center and the developer documentation for building keyboard-aware POS extensions.; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/getting-started/keyboard-shortcuts | text: developer documentation; href: https://pos.docs.shopify.io/pos/development/pos/ui-ux/external-keyboard/]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/scan-discount-codes-in-shopify-pos; date: April 27, 2026; title: Scan discount codes; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: Staff can now apply discount codes at checkout by scanning a QR code - no more typing long codes by hand. You can also generate scannable QR codes for any discount code from the Shopify admin, print them, share them with customers, or keep them at the counter for staff use. What's new - Generate QR codes in the admin: open any discount code and download a scannable QR code to share with customers or display in-store. - Scan to apply in POS: apply discounts in POS via the device camera or a connected hardware scanner. - Scan to apply online: share a QR with customers that they can use when shopping online. - Faster than typing: applying a discount by scan is meaningfully faster than typing codes on a keypad, which reduces checkout friction for staff. This update works with product-specific and order-level discount codes. Automatic discounts are not included (no code to scan). For developers & partners - QR codes encode the existing shareable link format: https://{shop}.myshopify.com/discount/{CODE} - the same URL Shopify has always used for shareable discount links. GS1 Digital Link is not used in this release. - If your app generates its own QR codes for Shopify discount codes, use this URL format so they're compatible with POS scanning. - Note: codes with special characters are URL-encoded twice by Shopify's route helper. For standard alphanumeric codes (e.g. SUMMER20) this is a no-op; for codes with special characters, match Shopify's double-encoding so POS can decode them correctly. Learn more about scanning discount codes in the Help Center.; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/discount-management/applying-discounts]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/u-s-retailers-can-adjust-retail-prices-on-shopify-collective; date: April 27, 2026; title: U.S. retailers can adjust retail prices on Shopify Collective; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Collective]; text: Retailers connected to suppliers on Shopify Collective have the option to turn off price sync and set their own retail price for imported products, above or below the supplier's listed price. Price sync remains on by default for all existing connections. Retailers must change this setting to adjust prices. Suppliers can view the retail price a retailer has set for their products on the order detail page. Supplier cost price is never affected by retail price changes made by the retailer. If you're a retailer with existing connections, we recommend reaching out to your suppliers before making retail price changes to align on expectations.; links: [text: change this setting; href: https://help.shopify.com//manual/online-sales-channels/shopify-collective/retailers/importing-products#product-pricing]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/use-matches-in-shopifyql-to-filter-by-what-customers-did; date: April 24, 2026; title: Use MATCHES in ShopifyQL to filter by what customers did; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Analytics]; text: We've added MATCHES to the ShopifyQL editor in Analytics so you can filter your reports by what customers did, not just who they are. You can now use MATCHES in the WHERE clause to filter by customer behavior. For example, you may want to see customers who purchased at least 2 products in the last 30 days. sql FROM customers SHOW customer_id, email WHERE products_purchased MATCHES (quantity >= 2, date >= -30d) GROUP BY customer_id The same MATCHES logic you use in Customer Segmentation works in Analytics, so your segments and reports stay consistent. For syntax, examples, and limitations, see the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/shopifyql-editor/shopifyql-syntax#where]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/compare-multiple-metrics-on-one-chart; date: April 23, 2026; title: Compare multiple metrics on one chart; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now plot multiple metrics on the same chart in Analytics. Add up to 4 metrics to a line chart to see how they trend together, or use the new "Bar and line" visualization to compare volume and rates side by side, all without toggling between charts. What's new: * Multi-metric line charts: Add up to 4 metrics to a single line chart using checkboxes in the config panel. Metrics with different value types (like dollar totals and percentages) automatically get their own Y-axis scale. * Bar and line charts: A new visualization type that plots one metric as bars and another as a line, useful for pairing metrics like Total Sales and Conversion Rate on a single chart. Where to find it: Available in explorations, saved reports, and dashboard cards. Learn more; links: [text: Learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/custom-reports/visualizations#multi-metric-visualizations]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/updates-to-local-pickup-user-experience-in-checkout; date: April 21, 2026; title: Updates to local pickup user experience in checkout; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Checkout]; text: Previously, checkout listed shipping and local pickup options vertically, creating a long scrollable list that made it hard for customers to quickly scan—especially for complex checkouts with multiple pickup locations. Checkout now displays the first available local pickup location with an option to view and select additional locations. No action is required to display these updates. Shipping and local pickup options now appear inline for easier selection Delivery method selection is determined by whether items in the cart is eligible for shipping or local pickup Local pickup only appears when items are pickup eligible, including when there are available pickup locations in the buyer's country Selecting local pickup shows the nearest location with item availability; a modal displays the full list You may want to review your checkout extension configuration to ensure any customizations still display correctly with these changes.; media: [tag: img; src: https://cdn.shopify.com/static/checkout/Checkout%20pickup%20changelog%20.png]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/spot-trends-with-new-analytics-insights; date: April 20, 2026; title: Spot trends with new Analytics insights; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Analytics insights are now available to merchants averaging 10 or more orders per week. If you meet this criteria, you'll now see automated data summaries directly on your Home feed. We have also expanded the data we analyze to include Sessions and Fulfillments. We now monitor over 80 new data combinations to help you spot trends without digging through reports. What you can now track: * Session Trends: Monitor changes in visitors, cart additions, and conversion rates. We now highlight patterns based on geographic location, referrer, device type, and landing page. * Fulfillment Efficiency: Automatically identify changes in fulfillment speeds and order volumes. You can now see performance breakdowns by shipping carrier, geographic location, and sales channel. Where to find it: Look for these insights to appear as cards on your Home feed when trends are detected. Learn more; links: [text: Learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/shopify-home#insights]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-most-relevant-sort-order-for-products-in-a-collection; date: April 15, 2026; title: New Most Relevant sort order for products in a collection; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: We've added Most Relevant as a collection sort order option. Your existing collections sorting remains unchanged and the new Most Relevant sort appears alongside your existing sort options like Bestselling, Price, and Newest. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-cash-management-foundations-for-shopify-pos; date: April 02, 2026; title: New Cash Management Foundations for Shopify POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: We rebuilt cash management across POS and the POS channel in Admin, and added new register extension targets and APIs. Track, control, and reconcile cash with register sessions, reason codes, and a new cash drawer and ledger model. What’s new in POS Updated Register UX: See a clear summary of each register session on device, including improved cash tracking, a breakdown of payments, and granular cash activity that shows when a drawer was opened and by which staff member. Native cash reason codes: Require a reason code for any non‑order cash activity (for example, opening the drawer or making adjustments). Enable and customize codes from the POS channel to get the audit trail you need. Open drawer setting: Control whether a device automatically opens the cash drawer after an order—useful for staff using mobile devices on the sales floor. What’s new in Admin (POS channel) Register sessions tab: A dedicated tab in Admin shows sessions opened and closed, and expected cash balances across locations and per location. Improved filtering and export make accounting and reconciliation faster. New Foundation, APIs, Extensions Cash drawer and ledger model: Multiple devices can contribute to a single cash drawer. Move beyond “one device = one session” with sessions across devices that roll up to one drawer via an updated data model and APIs. Payment reporting stays device‑level; cash reporting can span contributing devices with a ledger that provides full auditability of every cash event. Register extension targets: New POS targets let apps plug into open/close procedures, show alerts when balances exceed float/min/max thresholds, and enrich session details with custom logic or reporting. Automated workflows via API: Use APIs to open and close sessions programmatically, create cash drawers and reason codes, assign devices to a drawer, and pull custom reports. If you run multiple registers, share drawers across staff and devices, or need tighter control over how cash moves in and out of stores, these features give you more accountable, end‑to‑end cash tracking. Get started See Help Center for in‑app workflows. Read the developer changelog Explore POS UI extension targets; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/cash-register-management | text: changelog; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog/new-retail-cash-management-capabilities | text: POS UI extension targets; href: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/pos-ui-extensions/latest/targets/register-details]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/see-which-apps-use-extensions-and-functions-to-power-your-checkout-online-store-and-more; date: April 01, 2026; title: See which apps use Extensions and Functions to power your checkout, online store, and more; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now see exactly which app features are active across your store, which features are inactive, and which ones are collecting data through Pixels, so you can more confidently manage your apps. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/capital-remittance-via-shopify-payments-expands-to-all-states-of-the-us; date: April 01, 2026; title: Capital Remittance via Shopify Payments Expands to all states of the US; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Shopify Capital]; text: We’ve expanded Capital remittance via Shopify Payments to merchants across the rest of the U.S. This enhancement enables a smoother and more efficient remittance experience. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/visual-updates-to-checkout-blocks-app; date: March 31, 2026; title: Visual updates to Checkout Blocks app; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Checkout]; text: Starting today, we’re upgrading the Checkout Blocks app to the latest API version. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/schedule-and-test-storefront-changes-with-rollouts; date: March 31, 2026; title: Schedule and test storefront changes with Rollouts; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Rollouts bring experimentation and scheduling directly into your admin. With Rollouts, you can: Save theme changes and schedule them to go live at a specific date and time. Set an end date for limited-time events like flash sales and your store automatically reverts when the promotion ends. Run an A/B test to compare your changes against your current theme with real traffic, review the impact on conversions, and select the winning version. Target a Rollout to a specific market to run a regional promotion or test changes for a particular audience like a localized homepage for European buyers or a seasonal campaign for North America. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/create-pickup-orders-in-shopify-pos; date: March 30, 2026; title: Create pickup orders in Shopify POS; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Shopify POS v11.3 introduces the ability to create orders for future pickup directly in-store. Retail staff can now select Pickup as the delivery method when creating an order in POS, making it easier to sell items that customers will collect at a later date. This new workflow helps merchants support common retail scenarios like made-to-order products, tailored items, customized goods, or items that need to be transferred before fulfillment. Once a pickup order is created, staff can use Shopify POS’s existing pick and pack workflow to prepare and fulfill the order when it’s ready. Updates include: *Pickup as a delivery option in POS: *Staff can now create pickup orders directly from the POS device. *Built into existing fulfillment workflows: *Pickup orders can be fulfilled using the current pick and pack workflow in POS. *Supports future fulfillment: *Staff can sell items that are in stock now or expected to be available later. *A more consistent retail workflow: *Store teams can manage pickup orders in POS without relying on Shopify Admin or workarounds. This update closes a key gap between in-store selling and omnichannel fulfillment, giving retail teams a more reliable way to create and manage customer pickup orders directly from the sales floor. *Access: *Available in POS v11.3 when the “Pickup in store” fulfillment method is enabled in the store. Admins can also set the “Fulfill shipping and pickup orders” staff permission in their admin under Sales channels > Point of Sale to control which staff can manage pickup orders. This release supports pickup orders for the current location in POS. Learn more about creating and fulfilling pickup orders in the Help Center; links: [text: Learn more about creating and fulfilling pickup orders in the Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/order-management/pickup-in-store-for-online-orders]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/updated-list-of-tax-inclusive-countries-when-dynamic-tax-inclusive-pricing-is-used; date: March 27, 2026; title: Updated list of tax inclusive countries when dynamic tax-inclusive pricing is used; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [International]; text: Dynamic tax-inclusive pricing helps you offer a localized experience to customers in different countries. It does so by automatically updating your storefront prices to include the local tax rate in countries where tax-inclusive pricing is commonly used, if you are collecting taxes there. This change adds 17 additional countries where customers expect taxes to be included in prices. The countries that are being added to the list are Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Indonesia, Israel, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Peru, Philippines, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam. If you are not collecting tax in these countries, nothing will change for you or your customers. If your shop address is in any of these countries, nothing will change for your domestic customers, since dynamic tax-inclusive pricing only affects cross-border sales.; links: [text: Dynamic tax-inclusive pricing; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/pricing/dynamic-tax-inclusive-pricing]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/updates-to-setting-up-shipping-options; date: March 26, 2026; title: Updates to setting up shipping options; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Setting up shipping options, previously called rates, is now simpler and gives you more control and flexibility. Each option can now include a separate transit time and description. This allows you to give customers more details at checkout. You can now also offer free shipping by setting a minimum order value on a shipping option. This update lets you: * Set weight or price range conditions in a single shipping option * Add a custom description for each shipping option to display at checkout * Offer free shipping automatically when an order reaches a specified threshold For more details, learn about setting up shipping options.; links: [text: learn about setting up shipping options; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/setup/shipping-rates/setting-up-shipping-rates]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/run-a-deep-analysis-on-your-online-store-theme-with-simgym; date: March 26, 2026; title: Run a deep analysis on your online store theme with SimGym; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Apps]; text: SimGym now lets you analyze any single theme on its own. Instead of setting up a comparison between two themes, you can run a deep analysis and get feedback from AI-shoppers who browse your store like real customers would. You can focus the analysis on specific areas of your store, like your homepage, product pages, collection pages, or cart. You'll see what's working well and where there's room to improve, along with clear next steps you can act on right away. To get started, go to the SimGym app in your Shopify admin, select "Analyze a theme," choose any live or draft theme, and optionally pick the site areas you want to focus on. Learn more about analyzing a single theme using SimGym in our help documentation.; links: [text: help documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/simgym]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/customize-your-product-detail-pages-on-shop-with-blocks; date: March 25, 2026; title: Customize your product detail pages on Shop with blocks; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Shop]; text: We’ve added blocks in the Shop Editor so you can now add rich, branded sections below your product details — the same kind of customization you're used to on your online store. Your customizations appear on both the Shop mobile app and shop.app on the web. To get started, open the Shop channel in your Shopify admin and go to Shop Editor. Learn more about blocks in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shop Editor; href: https://admin.shopify.com/apps/shop-72/merchant/editor | text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/shop/manage-shop-store/customize/product-page]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/redesigned-theme-editor-navigation; date: March 25, 2026; title: Redesigned theme editor navigation; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Themes]; text: The theme editor has a new layout that puts your site preview front and center. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-new-actions-to-get-data-about-workflow-runs-abandoned-checkouts-inventory-items-catalogs-and-pages; date: March 24, 2026; title: Flow: New actions to get data about workflow runs, abandoned checkouts, inventory items, catalogs, and pages; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Apps]; text: Flow now has more actions to fetch data from your Shopify store to use in workflows. These "Get data" actions call a query with a set of filters and return a list of data that matches. Like other similar actions, these actions return a list of up to 100 resources. The Get workflow run data action retrieves information about a workflow run, including the workflow it belongs to, the event that triggered it, retry attempts, and timing details. Use this to build workflows that monitor or report on other workflow activity — for example, to track retry patterns or audit trigger sources. The Get abandoned checkout data action retrieves abandoned checkout information from your Shopify store. Abandoned checkouts are carts that a customer started but didn't complete. Use this to build workflows that follow up on lost sales, generate reports, or trigger recovery campaigns. The Get inventory item data action retrieves inventory item information from your Shopify store. Inventory items represent the physical goods that you track stock for. Use this to build workflows that monitor stock changes, and flag recently updated items. The Get page data action retrieves page information from your Shopify store. Pages are standalone content like About Us, Contact, or FAQ pages. Use this to build workflows that audit published content, track page updates, or manage your online store's static pages. For more information, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: Get workflow run data; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/get-workflow-run-data | text: Get abandoned checkout data; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/get-abandoned-checkout-data | text: Get inventory item data; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/get-inventory-item-data | text: Get page data; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/get-page-data | text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions | text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-more-of-shopify-s-admin-api-is-now-a-native-action; date: March 24, 2026; title: Flow: More fields from Shopify Admin API are available; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Apps]; text: Nearly all of Shopify's Admin API fields are now available natively in Flow, including those that requirement arguments to use, such as product.inCollection, which requires a collection ID to access. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shipping-and-delivery-settings-are-now-easier-to-scan; date: March 24, 2026; title: Shipping and delivery settings are now easier to scan; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: The Shipping and delivery settings page has been refreshed to help you find what you need faster. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/collect-marketing-consent-on-the-customer-sign-in-page; date: March 23, 2026; title: Collect marketing consent on the customer sign-in page; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Customer accounts]; text: The customer sign-in page now supports marketing consent collection. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/collect-credit-remittances-through-shopify-payments-in-texas; date: March 19, 2026; title: Collect Credit remittances through Shopify Payments in Texas; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: Due to new legal requirements in Texas, Shopify Credit began collecting remittances through Shopify Payments for all financings repaying from sales with the "Pay over Time from Sales" repayment method, starting January 12, 2026. For these financings, the repayment amount is automatically deducted from each day’s Shopify Payments payout before the payout is deposited into the merchant’s bank account. Please note: This change applies only to "Pay over Time from Sales" repayments. "Pay in Full" monthly repayments will continue to be collected through ACH direct debit.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/faster-discount-entry-in-pos; date: March 18, 2026; title: Faster discount entry in POS; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Discounts are one of the most common actions at the POS - now they’re faster and easier to apply, even during your busiest moments. We’ve streamlined the Manage discount experience in the Shopify POS app so staff can quickly find and apply the right discount without slowing down the line. Whether it’s a promo code or quick % off, everything is easier to access and faster to enter. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/smarter-international-pricing-with-managed-markets; date: March 03, 2026; title: Smarter international pricing with Managed Markets; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Adaptive pricing for Managed Markets automatically adjusts your international product prices to include duties, taxes, currency conversion, and merchant of record fees. This means customers see transparent, localized prices at checkout with no surprise charges, and your payout amounts stay consistent with your domestic orders. Learn more about adaptive pricing in the Shopify Help Center. How it works When you turn on adaptive pricing, we start from your domestic prices and automatically derive international prices for each market. Here's what we do behind the scenes: Convert to local currency using a stabilized exchange rate that we guarantee for a week - so your customers see consistent, predictable prices instead of numbers that change every hour Include duties and import taxes directly in the product price, so your customers pay one clear price at checkout with no surprise fees later Include Managed Markets and FX fees in the price, so your margins stay predictable Apply smart rounding to keep prices looking clean and natural in every currency The result: your international customers see localized, all-inclusive prices that feel just like buying from a local store. And your payouts work just like they do domestically -- you get your domestic price minus payment processing fees, and we handle the rest. What you see in your Shopify admin We've built new tools into your admin so you can see exactly what's happening with adaptive pricing: A toggle on each market's details page to turn adaptive pricing on or off per market A payout breakdown modal on the order details page that shows you how your payout amount is calculated - including the duties, taxes, FX, and fees that were included in the customer's price A pricing audit trail so you can see how each product's price was derived, from your domestic price through every adjustment Getting started Adaptive pricing is available now for all Managed Markets merchants powered by Shopify Payments. If you're new to Managed Markets, adaptive pricing is enabled by default when you onboard. If you're an existing Managed Markets merchant, you can turn it on from your admin: Go to Settings > Markets. Click on a market managed by Managed Markets. In the pricing section, toggle adaptive pricing on. That's it. We'll start deriving localized, all-inclusive prices for that market right away. A few things to keep in mind Adaptive pricing is available on Managed Markets powered by Shopify Payments. Merchants that joined after October 14, 2025 have access today; those that joined prior will gain access March 26, 2026. Prices are stabilized on a weekly cadence, so your customers see consistent pricing between updates. If you've set fixed prices for specific products in a market, they will not be adapted. You are responsible for ensuring they leave you with sufficient margin after duties, taxes, and cross border fees. Gift cards are excluded from adaptive pricing adjustments. Refunds are handled automatically. Duties and taxes included in the price are returned to you when recoverable. FX and Managed Markets fees are not returned. Order edits are supported - if you modify an order before fulfillment, the included duties and taxes are recalculated and any difference is credited or debited accordingly. You can turn adaptive pricing off at any time. When you do, your markets will revert to the standard duty-exclusive pricing model.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/managed-markets/adaptive-pricing]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/vat-number-validation-available-in-checkout; date: February 25, 2026; title: VAT number validation available in checkout; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: VAT Number Validation at Checkout Merchants using Shopify Tax in the European Union or United Kingdom can now enable VAT number validation at checkout to automatically apply the reverse charge exemption on eligible orders. We will be increasing availability over the next few weeks as we roll this out. Who this is for This applies to merchants who use Shopify Tax in the European Union or United Kingdom and have at least one fulfillment location in the European Union. Reverse charge eligibility is based on the order's fulfillment location country, not your store address. How to enable it In your checkout settings, set the Company VAT number field to Optional if you sell B2B to customers in the EU or UK. How the reverse charge exemption works When the exemption applies, VAT is removed from the order at checkout, and the customer is responsible for reporting and paying VAT on their own tax return. The exemption applies to: EU → EU shipments where the destination country differs from the fulfillment location country EU → UK shipments The exemption does not apply to: UK → EU shipments UK → UK shipments Example: You fulfill from France and ship to a customer in Ireland with a valid VAT number — the reverse charge exemption applies. Validation and customer data VAT numbers entered at checkout are automatically validated. The VAT numbers will be saved to the customer profile for future orders. VAT invoices If you enable the Company VAT number field, you may want to also enable VAT invoices so customers receive correct documentation. When the exemption is applied, the invoice includes: Reverse Charge Mechanism: Recipient responsible for VAT. Fraud prevention VAT number validation confirms formatting and validity at the time of check, but doesn't guarantee the customer is authorized to use the number. If you suspect fraudulent use — for example, the VAT number doesn't match the customer's company name or country — verify independently using the EU's VIES VAT number validation service and review the order before fulfilling. It's also possible that there have been too many attempts by a customer to validate a VAT number. In such cases, Shopify might enforce a rate limit to protect merchants from possible fraud. Multiple fulfillment locations If you have multiple locations, keep in mind that you can change which location fulfills an order, and this affects reverse charge eligibility since it's based on the fulfillment location country.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-pos-version-11-0; date: February 18, 2026; title: Shopify POS version 11.0; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: We’ve just launched Shopify POS version 11.0, bringing meaningful updates to the cart and core selling flow to help you and your staff work faster and stay focused during busy in-store moments. This release introduces improved cart interactions, add customer workflows, and smarter action handling, all built to make high frequency tasks easier and faster. The result is a more predictable staff experience that helps staff stay focused, oriented on the cart, and move faster through transactions with confidence, even if it's their first time using the POS. Here’s what’s new in version 11.0 Improved cart and action workflows - A cleaner, more readable cart layout makes it easier to scan items, prices and totals at a glance - The More actions menu now includes only actions that apply to the cart as a whole. Other actions have moved closer to where they’re used, either in the Smart Grid or directly in the cart. - Multi-select in the cart lets staff edit or modify multiple items at once, reducing repetitive actions on larger orders - Key actions including Customers and Staff attribution now open in a dedicated left side panel, reducing pop ups and keeping staff oriented during checkout Smarter Add customer flows - A smarter Add customer flow with better customer matching and autofill, making it easier to attach the right customer and avoid duplicate customer entries Faster, more consistent checkout - The cart remains visible throughout checkout, maintaining context from item selection through payment - Faster and clearer payment selection, so staff can move quickly between tender types - Larger number pads for cash and split payments, now displayed in the left side panel to reduce pop ups during checkout - Simplified split payment flow that’s easier to complete Refined post purchase experience - Clearer receipt selection and post purchase actions - Improved buyer facing screens and receipt selection on tablet and mobile, creating a more consistent experience for customers Performance and reliability improvements - Performance upgrades across search, product selection, and cart building - Faster checkout transitions and payment processing for a smoother end to end transaction Shopify POS app v11.0 represents a foundational upgrade to how staff build carts, complete checkout, and handle post purchase actions. These improvements work together to reduce friction across the core selling flow, helping staff move confidently through transactions and deliver the best possible in-store experience. See all the updates and more in the Retail Blog.; links: [text: Retail Blog; href: https://www.shopify.com/blog/retail-release-roundup]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/improved-us-sales-tax-reports; date: February 13, 2026; title: Improved United States sales tax reports; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: We added data fields and fixed calculations in two US sales tax reports used for filing and exports: the state-level Detailed transactions report and the Jurisdiction report. Detailed transactions report * Added full address details for each transaction: destination, origin, and billing. * Added product category and any tax exemptions applied to the transaction. Jurisdiction report * Added new columns showing combined item and shipping totals. * Fixed a calculation error: columns intended to show item totals no longer include shipping. Learn more about how each tax report is used or the data fields in the report.; links: [text: how each tax report is used; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/taxes/tax-reports | text: the data fields in the report; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/finances-report]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/use-metafields-as-dimensions-and-filters-in-analytics; date: February 12, 2026; title: Use metafields as dimensions and filters in Analytics; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Analytics]; text: We've released metafields in Analytics so you can use your custom data in reports. You can now group and filter by metafields on products, variants, customers, and orders, for example by material, loyalty tier, or ingredients, directly in Reports and Explore. No need to export to spreadsheets: your custom dimensions live in Analytics. Choose which metafields to use by turning on Use in Analytics in Settings → Metafields and metaobjects for each definition (Products, Variants, Customers, or Orders). We built this so you can segment and analyze the data that matters to your business without leaving Shopify. For step-by-step guidance and supported types, see the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/custom-data/options#list-of-options-available-for-metafields]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/create-customers-and-companies-with-sidekick; date: February 10, 2026; title: Create customers and companies with Sidekick; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Sidekick]; text: Sidekick can now create customers and companies for you. Describe what you need in plain language, and Sidekick fills out the forms automatically. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/sell-fixed-bundles-on-google; date: February 10, 2026; title: Sell fixed bundles on Google; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Channels]; text: Fixed bundles (a set bundle with fixed components) can now be published to Google. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/collect-capital-remittance-through-shopify-payments-in-texas; date: February 09, 2026; title: Collect Capital remittance through Shopify Payments in Texas; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Shopify Capital]; text: Due to new legal requirements in Texas, Shopify Capital began collecting repayments through Shopify Payments for new financing originated on or after September 1, 2025. For these financings, the repayment amount is automatically deducted from each day’s Shopify Payments payout before the payout is deposited into the merchant’s bank account. Please note: This change applies only to new Shopify Capital loans or Capital Flex accounts originated on or after September 1, 2025. Repayments for financings originated before this date will continue to be collected through ACH direct debit.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/australia-post-account-linking-available-on-grow-and-basic-plans; date: February 09, 2026; title: Australia Post account linking available on Grow and Basic plans; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Merchants on Grow and Basic plans in Australia can now connect their Australia Post account to Shopify at no additional cost. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/sending-payment-requests-per-fulfillment; date: February 06, 2026; title: Sending payment requests per fulfillment; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Orders]; text: With payment requests per fulfillment, you can manage cash flow for orders with mixed lead times, collect payment on pre-orders as they arrive, and ship in-stock items without waiting for backordered products. Your buyers can pay through Customer Accounts, where unpaid requests appear directly, or via the payment link in email. This is particularly valuable if you're managing pre-orders, custom products, or seasonal inventory where items ship at different times. Instead of manually tracking partial payments outside of Shopify, you can request payment for each shipment as it goes out, all tracked directly in your admin. Learn more about sending payment requests per fulfillment in the Shopify Help Center. Exclusive to Plus.; links: [text: sending payment requests per fulfillment; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders/payments/deferred-payments#payment-per-fulfillment]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/fulfilling-transfers-with-shopify-pos; date: February 02, 2026; title: Fulfilling Transfers with Shopify POS; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Shopify POS 10.20 introduces a complete inventory transfers workflow to the POS device. Retail staff can now fulfill (outgoing) and receive (incoming) inventory transfers between locations natively—no need to rely solely on Shopify Admin or external apps. Staff can now pick, pack and send shipments using Outgoing Transfers under the Orders tab. Verify and receive incoming shipments under the Products tab. Staff can scan items to confirm inventory movement, track transfer status in real time, and operate with improved accuracy right from the sales floor. Updates include: - Outgoing transfers: HQ can assign transfers in Admin; retail staff can pick, pack, and send transfers right from POS. - All-in-one workflow: Outgoing transfers are under Orders and incoming under Products, all within POS. - Greater traceability: Scan, verify, and track transfers for better control. Status is tracked in Shopify for reporting and auditing. - User permissions: Easily choose which staff members can manage transfers. - Direct Integration: Outgoing and incoming transfers are built directly into Shopify’s existing inventory management system—no additional apps or setup required. These enhancements streamline in-store inventory operations, reduce the risk of overselling, and help your in-store teams maintain accurate stock levels across all locations. Learn more about fulfilling transfers with POS.; links: [text: Learn more about fulfilling transfers with POS; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/inventory-management/fulfilling-and-receiving-transfers]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-send-emails-using-your-sender-email-address; date: January 31, 2026; title: Flow: Send emails using your sender email address; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Apps]; text: The Send internal email action in Shopify Flow will now display the sender email address for your store in the From field of the email. Before this change, the action would display “flow@shopify.com” in the From field. To ensure emails are sent correctly, go to Settings > Notifications in your Shopify admin and ensure the sender email is properly configured. If you use a third-party domain, then you may need to authenticate your sender email address to prevent your emails messages from being flagged as spam and ensure that your email messages are delivered. Email recipients may also need to update their email filtering or forwarding rules to match the sender email address instead of "flow@shopify.com". Update: this work has been completed as of March 11th, 2026. For more information, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: Send internal email; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/send-email | text: sender email address; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/intro-to-shopify/initial-setup/setup-your-email#change-your-sender-email-address | text: Notifications; href: https://admin.shopify.com/settings/notifications | text: authenticate your sender email address; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/intro-to-shopify/initial-setup/setup-your-email#authenticate | text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/send-email | text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/c/shopify-flow/304]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/updates-to-chargeback-rates; date: January 28, 2026; title: Updated Chargeback Rate Calculation; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Analytics]; text: Starting Jan 28th, we're updating chargeback rate calculations across all of Shopify, including your admin dashboard, analytics, and notifications, to provide a more complete and consistent view of your chargeback risk. What's Changing The updated chargeback rate metric now includes all disputes, including those resolved through programs like Visa's Rapid Dispute Resolution (RDR). You'll also be able to use the RDR filter in reports to see the traditional view (without RDR). This gives you a fuller picture of your chargeback activity and helps you track risk more accurately. There are no changes to how Shopify evaluates risk. Why This Matters With these updates, you'll have the accurate information to monitor chargeback risk and take action before elevated chargebacks impact your business. Learn more about managing chargebacks in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shopify-payments/managing-chargebacks]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/control-how-your-retail-locations-are-classified; date: January 28, 2026; title: Control how your retail locations are classified; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: We’ve added a physical storefront toggle to Locations in Shopify Admin, so retail locations are no longer inferred solely from POS activity and can be explicitly defined. Now you can clearly separate customer facing stores from POS-only locations like pop-ups, test locations, or warehouses using a single control. This improves location discovery across channels like Shop and keeps analytics, reporting, and future location-based features accurate and reliable. Location names shown to customers in Shop will match the location name in Admin, so we recommend reviewing your location names. The physical storefront toggle is enabled by default. Learn more about managing physical storefronts and POS locations in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/getting-started/shopify-pos-from-admin/add-locations]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/change-due-calculator-for-cash-payments; date: January 27, 2026; title: Change due calculator for cash payments; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: When a customer pays with cash in quick sale, you can now enter the amount they give you and instantly see the change due. No more mental math at the register. The calculator also supports cash rounding for markets that have eliminated small coin denominations. It automatically rounds the total and calculates change based on the rounded amount. How it works: * Complete a cash sale in quick sale * Enter the amount the customer gives you * See the change due instantly * Change amount appears on receipts and order confirmation Available on iOS and Android in all quick sale markets. Learn more at Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-mobile/quick-sale]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/business-details-section-in-admin-general-settings; date: January 22, 2026; title: Improved clarity for managing Business details; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now manage your store’s business details in the General settings page with an updated Business details section. This makes it easier to keep the information Shopify needs for verification and financial services up to date—without having to wait for onboarding or remediation. We’ve renamed the Billing address section in Store contact details to Store address to better reflect what that address represents. This does not change how your address is used. Your store’s currency is now set based on the business country selected in Business details. Note: If you have financial products such as Shopify Payments or Shopify Capital active you will need to deactivate these before making changes.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/improved-product-availability-for-market-specific-inventory; date: January 20, 2026; title: Improved product availability for market-specific inventory; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Inventory]; text: As of January 2026, products with available inventory in a buyer's market can now be purchased at checkout, even if inventory is negative or zero at other locations. Previously, negative total stock in all locations, including retail locations, could cause products to appear sold out and block checkout, even when the buyer's market had inventory in stock. Now, checkout considers only the inventory at locations that can actually fulfill orders for the buyer's market.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/offline-payments-for-multi-entity; date: January 19, 2026; title: Offline payments for multi entity; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: We’ve added offline payments support to multi-entity Shopify Payment setups, so offline transactions now work across all shops. Transaction limits are automatically inherited instead of configured per entity with no additional configurations required. Now you can keep selling during connectivity issues even if your business operates more than one operational entity across multiple shops. Learn more about https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/selling-offline/offline-payments?mode=internal in the Shopify Help Center.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/enhanced-return-reasons; date: January 16, 2026; title: Better insights with category-specific return reasons; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Understanding why customers return products is key to improving your business. We've enhanced return reasons to give you richer, more actionable data about every return. What's new When processing returns, you'll now see suggested return reasons that are specific to the product being returned. Instead of generic options, you'll get relevant choices for each product category—like "Too big" or "Too small" for apparel, or "Taste," "Style," and "Weight" for items where those attributes matter. These suggestions are powered by Shopify's Standard Product Taxonomy and are available everywhere you process returns: - Shopify admin - Point of Sale (POS) - Shopify self-serve returns - The Shop app Why it matters Better return reasons mean better data. With more specific and consistent return information, you can: - Reduce future returns by addressing product issues faster (like sizing problems or quality concerns) - Make informed decisions about inventory and product development Return reasons are localized and standardized across your sales channels, so you'll get consistent insights whether returns happen online, in-store, or through self-serve customer accounts. Getting started Enhanced return reasons are available automatically—no setup needed. Buyers will see these new, product-specific options when creating returns through self-serve returns or the Shop app, while staff will see them in Shopify admin and POS. Simply process returns as usual to benefit from improved insights.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-adopts-version-2026-01-of-the-graphql-admin-api; date: January 15, 2026; title: Flow adopts version 2026-01 of the GraphQL Admin API; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Apps]; text: Flow now uses version 2026-01 of the GraphQL Admin API, which includes new options for building automations. Some of the changes in version 2026-01 of the GraphQL Admin API include: Advanced querying of metafields and metaobjects: We've expanded the resources that you can query by metafield value to include Companies and Company Locations. We've also expanded how you can query metafield values on Products, Orders, and Metaobject entries to include greater than and less than comparisons, prefix matching, and boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT). (changelog) Access transactions on the Return object: You can now access transaction data directly on the Return object that is included on triggers related to returns. (changelog) New return reason definitions: You can now use the new ReturnReasonDefinition type to capture more granular, category-specific return reasons when managing returns. This replaces the previous ReturnReason on the Return object that is included on triggers related to returns. The returnCreate and returnRequest mutations also accept this field as an input when using the mutation in a Send Admin API request action. (changelog) orderUpdate mutation now includes phone field: This field allows merchants to update the customer phone number for an order, overwriting the existing phone number, when using the mutation in a Send Admin API request action. (changelog) For more information about how Flow uses the GraphQL, visit the documentation. To learn more about changes introduced in version 2026-01, visit the Developer changelog.; links: [text: changes; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog?filter=api&api_version=2026-01&api_type=admin-graphql | text: changelog; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog/advanced-metafield-metaobject-querying | text: changelog; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog/access-transactions-on-the-return-object | text: changelog; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog/new-return-reason-definitions-api-for-better-return-insights | text: changelog; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog/order-update-phone-field-public | text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/getting-started/concepts/admin-api | text: Developer changelog; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog?filter=api&api_version=2026-01&api_type=admin-graphql]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/storefronts-are-getting-faster-and-ready-to-evolve; date: January 13, 2026; title: Updates to how Shopify handles Liquid code; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Themes]; text: Starting January 13, 2026, we're updating how Shopify handles Liquid code in your theme files.
