uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-default-setting-for-pixel-data-sharing; date: January 13, 2026; title: New default setting for marketing pixel data sharing; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: In order to protect your store from accidentally oversharing data, Shopify will soon default to automatic data sharing optimization that monitors your marketing pixels and only shares data with tools that are driving results for your store. We see many pixels that haven’t sent traffic or sales to a merchant in weeks, months, or even years, and this feature is designed to protect your store from that exact situation if you forget to turn off sharing with inactive tools. We will look at multiple signals, including traffic and sales, to determine if sharing data back to a specific tool is helpful for your business. When we see zero signals coming from a pixel over days or weeks, we will pause data sharing until we see new signals, at which point data sharing turns back on. You’ll see the setting enabled immediately for all active marketing pixels, but it will not begin limiting data for pixels that aren’t driving results for at least the next seven days. To opt out of optimized data sharing, you can adjust pixel settings in Settings > Customer events, and set pixels to ‘always on’ to maintain full data sharing at all times.; links: [text: Settings > Customer events; href: https://admin.shopify.com/settings/customer_events]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/better-way-to-match-shopify-payments-payouts-with-bank-deposits; date: January 08, 2026; title: Better way to match Shopify Payments payouts with bank deposits; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Payments]; text: We’ve made it easier to match payouts to bank deposits and transactions to payouts in the exports. Payout export now include Bank Reference, and order transactions export now include Payout ID, so it's easier to confirm which bank deposit a payout relates to and see which transactions were included in each payout. This update is available to all Shopify Payments merchants. Learn more about exporting payouts and order transactions in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shopify-payments/payouts/view-details]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/bulgarian-lev-bgn-is-now-replaced-with-euros-eur; date: January 07, 2026; title: Euros (EUR) have replaced the Bulgarian Lev (BGN); tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: On Jan 1 2026, Bulgaria changed its official currency for electronic transactions from the Bulgarian Lev (BGN) to the Euro (EUR). As part of this change, markets that previously used the Bulgarian Lev have been updated to use Euros for stores that use Shopify's multi-currency feature. Customers previously paying in Bulgarian Lev will now pay in Euros. Shopify strongly recommends that stores who do not use multi-currency and currently have Bulgarian Lev as their default currency update their default currency to Euros. You can read more about this change on the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/markets-new/bulgaria-currency-transition]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/greater-flexibility-for-inventory-transfers; date: January 06, 2026; title: Greater flexibility for inventory transfers; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Inventory]; text: Managing inventory should be straightforward. Now, inventory transfers give you more control: Edit shipments anytime: Add, remove, or adjust items in a shipment—even after it’s in transit or received. Fix mistakes or update shipments as your plans change. Receive inventory without providing an origin: Leave the origin blank to record stock from sources outside Shopify—like purchase order suppliers, or unexpected deliveries. Use the reduced API restrictions and referenceName to link these transfers to external systems, so you can track and receive all your inventory through Shopify. Remove inventory to an unspecified destination: Write off, discard, or send inventory to places Shopify doesn’t track—like third-party warehouses, mobile teams, or suppliers—by leaving the destination blank. Keep track of your outbound inventory for later auditability. Every change appears in your adjustment history, so your records stay accurate and auditable. Important: The Transfer Update API no longer requires both an origin and destination. Review your integrations to see if your setup can benefit from the relaxed requirements. Learn more about inventory transfers in the Shopify Help Center and see our API docs for technical details.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/ | text: API docs; href: https://shopify.dev/docs/api]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-duties-and-import-taxes-us-section-232-tariff-customization; date: October 29, 2025; title: Shopify Duties and Import Taxes: US Section 232 tariff customization; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [International]; text: The United States applies additional tariffs on all HTSUS codes that represent products that may contain steel and aluminum, depending on the amount of metal in the product. By default, US Customs and Border Control will assume these products contain 100% metal unless it is specified differently on the commercial invoice. Previously, our duties and import tax calculations in checkout applied the same default - assume those products contain 100% metal. Now, duties and import taxes supports customizing the percentages of your product's value that Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs apply to. This new setting applies to all items in your store that fall under Section 232. To customize this amount, visit your admin's duty settings and enter the percentage in "United States Section 232 percentage". To ensure you also recieve a reduced rate when shipping your orders, ensure you also update your commercial invoices to reflect your product's proportion of metal. You can learn more about collecting duties and import taxes at checkout on the help center.; links: [text: collecting duties and import taxes at checkout; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/duties-and-import-taxes/index]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-cancel-in-progress-workflow-runs; date: October 29, 2025; title: Flow: Cancel in-progress workflow runs; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Apps]; text: You can now cancel workflow runs while they're in progress, either while they are executing a wait step, or when they are retrying due to an error. Because workflow runs can retry automatically for up to 36 hours after a transient error is encountered, before this update you could not rerun your workflow until the retries stopped. Now you can take control and cancel these runs immediately. For any run that’s currently in progress, you can cancel workflow runs on the workflow run details page. You can also cancel one or more runs from the “Recent runs” section on the workflow’s summary page. In addition, when you turn off a workflow, it will now cancel in progress runs. Once cancelled, you can rerun the workflow with any fixes made to your workflow. This gives you faster feedback loops when building and testing automations, and ensures failures don't block your workflow development. For more information, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/manage/monitor#cancelling-runs | text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/c/shopify-flow/304]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/filter-out-bot-traffic-in-your-sessions-related-reports; date: October 27, 2025; title: Filter out bot traffic in your sessions related reports; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Analytics]; text: You can now filter between human and bot traffic in your Shopify Analytics reports, giving you clearer insights into actual customer behavior. What's new: * “Human or Bot session” filter separates real customers from automated traffic * “Human or Bot session” dimension to drill down into human or bot specific patterns * More accurate metrics by focusing on genuine visitor behavior Get clearer conversion rates, identify which referral sources bring real customers, and measure true store performance without bot traffic skewing your data. How to use it: Open any Shopify Analytics sessions report and use the "Human or bot session" filter to focus on the traffic type most relevant to your analysis. Filter to "Human" to see your customer conversion rates, or view both to understand your complete traffic composition. Or, add it as a dimension to analyze the differences. Coming soon: Support for headless and Hydrogen stores Enhanced classification as the system continues learning from traffic patterns Learn more; links: [text: Learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/intro-to-shopify/bots/bot-filtering]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/test-orders-no-longer-sync-to-avalara-avatax; date: October 27, 2025; title: Test orders no longer sync to Avalara Tax Compliance; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Partners]; text: Merchants using Avalara Tax Compliance will no longer see test orders (orders created using a test payment gateway) appear in their Avalara AvaTax dashboard or reports. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/quick-count-extension-in-shopify-pos; date: October 23, 2025; title: Quick count extension in Shopify POS; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [POS]; text: With the new quick count extension in Shopify POS, you can now update your on hand inventory right from your POS app. Use your device’s built-in camera, a connected barcode scanner, or search for products by name—making the inventory process faster and less prone to errors. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-reporting-will-give-you-insights-into-cross-border-sales-profitability; date: October 22, 2025; title: New reporting will give you insights into cross border sales profitability; tags: [text: New]; areas: [International]; text: New reports called “Average profit margin by market” and “Profit margin by order” have been introduced to Shopify’s Reporting Platform. “Average profit margin by market” helps you understand how much profit you’re earning, per market. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shop-channel-updates-shoppable-videos-and-posts-migration; date: October 16, 2025; title: Shop channel updates: Shoppable videos and posts migration; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Shop]; text: Update: We've removed shoppable videos and shoppable posts from Shop product pages and Shop Stores as of October 15th, 2025. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/refund-payment-screen-in-pos; date: October 14, 2025; title: Refund screen for returns & exchanges; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Retail staff now have a dedicated refunds screen during the return and exchange checkout, designed to improve accuracy and revenue retention in the refund process. With this new screen, staff are no longer defaulted to the original payment method for refunds. Instead, they are presented with revenue-retaining options such as issuing a gift card or store credit directly from the refund flow. This screen also allows staff to accurately direct refunds or gift cards to the correct recipient—crucial for preventing errors like refunding to the original buyer instead of the intended recipient, especially for gifted orders. With this update: Staff can more easily promote revenue-retaining options to buyers, instead of always refunding to the original payment method. Misdirected refunds—such as accidentally issuing refunds to the original buyer’s credit card or sending digital gift cards to the wrong email due to pre-populated fields—are eliminated. Learn more about processing refunds in POS.; links: [text: processing refunds in POS.; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/order-management/complete-refund-orders]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/subscriptions-now-available-in-pos; date: October 14, 2025; title: Subscriptions now available in POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: You can now sell subscriptions in-store with Shopify POS using the Shopify Subscriptions app. This brings the same subscription options you offer online into your retail stores, so customers can start recurring purchases no matter where they shop. With this update, staff can add subscription products directly at checkout in POS. Buyers can subscribe in-store to the same plans available online, helping you drive repeat revenue and build lasting customer relationships. For developers, build custom subscription experiences using new properties added to the Cart API and LineItem interface. Learn more about API and extension updates in the developer changelog. Subscriptions on POS are available to all merchants using the Shopify Subscription app. Learn more about setup in the Help Center.; links: [text: developer changelog; href: https://shopify.dev/changelog/subscription-selling-plan-support-with-pos-ui-extensions | text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/payment-management/subscriptions]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/view-in-progress-returns-and-cancel-unfulfilled-items-in-pos-order-details; date: October 14, 2025; title: View in-progress returns and cancel unfulfilled items in POS order details; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: POS staff now have enhanced visibility into return processes and better tools for managing unfulfilled orders. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/country-specific-hs-code-management-for-international-selling; date: October 13, 2025; title: Country-specific HS code management for international selling; tags: [text: New]; areas: [International]; text: You can now enter country-specific Harmonized System (HS) codes for your products, giving you more control over customs classification and tariff calculations for each destination market. Your codes and Managed Markets codes are kept separate, so you always know which rates and rules apply.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-duties-and-import-taxes-usa-postal-rates-support; date: October 08, 2025; title: Shopify Duties and Import Taxes: USA postal tariff rate support; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [International]; text: Duties and import taxes now support a new option for postal tariff rate calculations for orders shipping into the United States. Previously, tariff rates for parcels using commercial and postal carriers were the same. As such, for packages shipping into the United States, the Shopify duties and import tax calculator calculates duties based on individual Harmonized System Code and Country of Origin information applied to your products. This calculation scheme is used by US Customs for commercial carriers, and is the default option. Now, with our new setting, merchants have the option to modify duties calculation towards postal tariff rates. When on, duty calculations are calculated Ad Valorem based on the Country Code of Origin of your products. This calculation scheme is appropriate if you ship with a postal carrier, like Canada Post. This new setting applies to all international checkouts with United States as the destination, regardless of available shipping options. To toggle the feature, visit your admin’s duty settings and click the box next to “Use postal duty rates into the United States”. For more information on Shopify Duties and Import Taxes, please see the help center.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-adopts-version-2025-10-of-the-graphql-admin-api; date: October 08, 2025; title: Flow adopts version 2025-10 of the GraphQL Admin API; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Apps]; text: Flow now uses version 2025-10 of the GraphQL Admin API, which includes new options for building automations. (Developer changelog) New fields for PaymentSchedule including balanceDue, totalBalance, and due. (Developer changelog) Rerouting fulfillment orders is now possible with the fulfillmentOrdersReroute mutation. You can redirect orders to different locations based on your business rules. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/turn-business-questions-into-analytics-reports-with-natural-language-queries; date: October 08, 2025; title: Turn business questions into analytics reports with Sidekick; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Sidekick]; text: The analytics query editor now integrates with Sidekick and understands natural language, making advanced reporting accessible to everyone. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/waive-outstanding-order-balances; date: October 29, 2026; title: Waive outstanding order balances; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: New release: You can now waive an order’s payable balance directly from the payment card on the order page when you choose not to collect it. You can also remove an existing waived amount from this page. Automatic adjustments: Shopify adjusts existing waived amounts when needed during order editing, refunds, and returns processing. If the order total falls below the waived amount, Shopify reverses only the excess, starting with the oldest waived amount. Clear buyer visibility: Waived balances appear wherever applicable across buyer-facing surfaces, including customer accounts, checkout, and email notifications. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/admin-supports-gtin-suggestions-and-autocomplete; date: October 29, 2026; title: Admin supports GTIN suggestions and autocomplete.; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: A GTIN is the globally unique number behind most retail barcodes, and sales channels like Google use it to match your listings to the right product. Shopify now checks your barcodes against the GS1 registry, the organization that issues GTINs, and helps you mark the ones that are real. What's new Autocomplete as you type: When you add a new barcode that looks like a GTIN, Shopify looks it up in the GS1 registry. If your GTIN is registered with GS1, the barcode is marked as GTIN for you, with a highlight so you can see what changed. Suggestions for barcodes you've already saved: Saved Custom barcodes that look like GTINs show a suggestion. Accept it to change the type to GTIN, or dismiss it. A heads-up when the registry disagrees: If GS1 has the barcode registered to a product, hover over it to compare your vendor and product name with GS1's record. This is for your information only. You don't need to change your product title, vendor or description to match GS1. Accept suggestions in bulk: In the products and inventory bulk editors, accept every GTIN suggestion at once, or dismiss them all. What stays the same Nothing here blocks you from saving. Shopify never changes a barcode you've already saved unless you accept the suggestion. You can still choose any barcode type yourself, including Custom for internal codes. GTIN suggestions, autocomplete and registry warnings are only signals to help you check your barcodes. Ignoring them won't affect your products or how you manage them in Shopify. Learn more about multiple barcodes on product variants.; links: [text: multiple barcodes on product variants; href: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/multiple-barcodes-in-variants]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/identify-more-in-store-customers-with-pos; date: October 28, 2026; title: Identify more in-store customers with POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: Shopify POS now recognizes eligible in-store shoppers who have previously checked out at a store powered by Shopify Payments, a network of hundreds of millions of buyers. When a buyer chooses to receive a digital receipt to their Shop app, by email, or by text, the purchase is connected to a customer profile and saved to your customer list, without staff asking for contact details at the register. Buyers can choose a digital receipt and to share their details with you in just one tap, and you can identify more in-store customers shopping with you without holding up the line asking for an email or phone number. The more in-store customers you know, the more you can invest in those relationships. Identifying more customers at checkout grows your customer list and gives you a foundation to market to them (if they've opted in to marketing), personalize their experience, and give them a reason to return. This is available in v11.17 of the POS app and works with Shopify Payments for POS when you have Shopify Network Intelligence enabled in your settings in admin. If you have a buyer-facing display, Customer View must be running v11.17 or later, no other action is required. If you do not have a buyer-facing display, you need to enable customer receipt selection in the Shopify admin.; links: [text: Shopify Network Intelligence; href: http://help.shopify.com/en/manual/privacy-and-security/privacy/customer-privacy-settings/privacy-settings#network-intelligence | text: customer receipt selection; href: http://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/receipt-management/customer-receipt-selection#manage-customer-receipt-selection]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/map-product-data-by-sales-channel; date: October 28, 2026; title: Map product data by sales channel; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Channels]; text: A new channel mapping page lets you manage and optimize the product data sent to each sales channel. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/see-activity-from-your-apps-in-shopify-analytics; date: October 28, 2026; title: See activity from your apps in Shopify Analytics; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Analytics]; text: You can now view events from supported apps directly in Shopify Analytics. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-flow-product-updated-trigger; date: October 28, 2026; title: Shopify Flow: Product updated trigger; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Apps]; text: You can now build workflows that respond when a product or product variant is updated on your shop with the “Product updated” trigger. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-flow-staff-now-need-permissions-to-test-and-turn-on-workflows; date: October 28, 2026; title: Shopify Flow: Staff now need permissions to test and turn on workflows; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Apps]; text: Shopify Flow now uses the staff permissions you manage in your Shopify admin. Before this change, a single Flow app permission let a staff member do everything in Flow. Now, access to Flow is set by the Flow automations permissions (“View, create, and delete automations” and “Manage connections and secrets”) in Settings > Users > Roles. Flow also checks each workflow against the staff member's other admin permissions. To test or turn on a workflow, staff need the permissions for each of its steps. For example, a workflow with the Add customer tags action needs the Edit customers permission. This makes sure staff can only do in Flow what their admin permissions already allow. Staff who are missing a permission that a workflow needs: Can still open Flow, build and edit workflows, and save drafts. Can't test, turn on, turn off, or apply changes to that workflow, run it manually, or cancel or retry its runs. Won't see data they don't have permission to view, such as sample data, test results, and workflow run details. Will see a message in Flow showing why they cannot access a feature. A few things to note: Workflows that are already on keep running. Staff who have access to Flow today keep it. They're given the Flow automations permissions automatically. Store owners always have full access to Flow. Workflows that use a connection or secret also need the Manage connections and secrets permission. To review what your staff can do, go to Settings > Users> Roles in your Shopify admin. When staff are missing a permission, Flow shows them what's missing when they attempt to access a feature. For more information, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: documentation; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/getting-started/staff-permissions/ | text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/c/shopify-flow/304]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/get-sidekick-recommendations-using-supported-app-data; date: October 28, 2026; title: Sidekick suggestions now work with supported apps; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Sidekick can use data from installed apps that have supported Sidekick app extensions to make suggestions based on fuller store context. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/knowledge-base-is-now-available-in-your-admin; date: October 26, 2026; title: Knowledge base is now built into your admin; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Knowledge base is now built into your Shopify admin at Sales channels > Agentic > Knowledge base. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-eu-product-identifiers-supported-on-shopify-shipping-managed-markets-labels; date: October 24, 2026; title: New EU Product identifiers supported on Shopify Shipping & Managed Markets labels; tags: [text: New]; areas: [International]; text: Upcoming regulatory changes Effective November 1, 2026, the EU requires three product identifiers for each item in direct-to-consumer parcels valued under €150. Parcels missing this information may be rejected at customs and incur return-to-origin fees. When you buy labels through Shopify Shipping or Managed Markets, Shopify adds these identifiers to your customs documents using your product data. Labels for EU-bound orders cannot be purchased for items missing required identifiers. What you need to do Add product identification information in Shopify in product barcodes. Learn more about adding barcodes to products. * Merchant Product Identifier (M-PID): No action needed. Your product variant in Shopify already covers this. * Standardized Product Identifier (S-PID): Add a barcode with type GTIN, EAN, UPC, or ISBN. If your product doesn't have one, declare that none exists on the product details page. * Non-Standardized Manufacturer Product Identifier (NS-PID): Add the manufacturer's model number, part number, or style code as a barcode with type NS-PID. You can also use your own product code or SKU. If you've added a standardized identifier but no NS-PID, Shopify uses the standardized identifier as the NS-PID. What's new Identifiers on EU customs documents. Shopify includes the required identifiers on labels and customs documents for parcels shipping into the EU, for both Managed Markets & Shopify Shipping. Declare when no standardized identifier exists. Mark products that don't have a standardized identifier from the product details page. Automatic exemptions. Shopify uses HS codes to identify exempt products and applies the exemption for you. Bulk updates. Add barcodes and declarations to many products at once in the bulk editor. If you buy labels outside of Shopify, contact your carrier, broker, or fulfillment partner to find out how to provide this information. Learn more in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: adding barcodes to products; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/add-update-products#adding-barcodes | text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/shipping/eu-product-identifiers]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/guaranteed-flat-rate-shipping-now-in-managed-markets; date: October 24, 2026; title: Guaranteed flat-rate shipping, now with Managed Markets; tags: [text: New]; areas: [International]; text: Managed Markets can now manage your international shipping rates alongside duty-inclusive pricing, giving buyers a simple shipping rate at checkout and protecting you from unexpected label adjustments. You can preview prices, checkout totals, and payouts before you turn it on. What’s new * Shipping rates managed for you. Managed Markets sets Standard and Express rates for each destination. Part of the shipping cost is included in your product prices, with the rest charged as shipping at checkout. Optionally absorb a portion of the cost for even lower buyer-facing prices. * Guaranteed label costs. Buy qualifying prepaid FedEx or DHL Express labels through Managed Markets, and you won’t be billed for later carrier cost adjustments. * Preview the full breakdown. See international product prices, checkout totals, and expected payouts for each market. Duty-inclusive pricing is required. Managed Markets sets and updates these shipping rates; you can’t edit them yourself. You can turn the feature off per market to use your own rates, without the label-cost guarantee. To review your settings, go to Markets, open a market, and find the Managed Markets section. Learn more in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/managed-markets/shipping/set-up-shipping]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/generate-images-with-transparent-backgrounds-in-sidekick; date: October 23, 2026; title: Generate images with transparent backgrounds in Sidekick; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Sidekick]; text: Sidekick can now generate images with transparent backgrounds. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/more-accurate-uk-vat-based-on-fulfillment-location; date: October 23, 2026; title: More accurate UK VAT based on fulfillment location; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: VAT on orders shipping to customers in Great Britain is now calculated using the fulfillment location that your order routing settings select for each order, the same way tax is calculated for orders shipping to the United States. If an order totals more than £135 GBP before tax and shipping and is routed to a location outside the UK, then the order is treated as an import, so VAT isn't charged at checkout. This applies even if your store also has a UK location. Orders of £135 GBP or less, orders shipping to Northern Ireland, and existing orders aren't affected. To charge VAT on these orders at checkout, update your order routing so they're assigned to a UK location, or collect duties and import taxes at checkout. Learn more about charging VAT on orders over £135 in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: charging VAT on orders over £135; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/taxes/uk/uk-tax-migrate#charge-vat-over-thresholdhttp://]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-protection-against-unexpected-redirects; date: October 20, 2026; title: New protection against unexpected redirects; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Online Store]; text: Update (October 23, 2026): Your online store now only blocks links to websites that Shopify has identified as malicious and asks for confirmation for websites that are suspicious. Otherwise, customers go directly to other websites without seeing a message. Your online store now asks customers to confirm before it sends them to a website outside your store. Domains that are connected to your store and supported Shopify and social websites don't trigger the message. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/create-manage-and-review-stock-counts-in-shopify-admin; date: October 20, 2026; title: Create, manage and review stock counts in Shopify admin; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Inventory]; text: Stock counts give you a structured way to verify inventory in Shopify admin. Create a count, have staff record what’s on the shelf using barcode scanning or manual entry, then review results before stock levels change. If you currently count using spreadsheets or manual workarounds, stock counts keeps the entire workflow in Shopify admin, with a clear record of what was counted, who counted it, and what changed. What’s available: * Create and schedule stock counts in admin * Add products manually using search or with barcode scanning * Assign counts to staff who can complete them in admin or POS * Multiple staff members can contribute to the same count without overriding each other * See who recorded each quantity and track count progress from creation to completion * Review variances between counted and recorded quantities before approving changes * New permissions settings to control who can perform counts and who can review and approve them Learn more about stock counts in the Shopify help center; links: [text: Shopify help center; href: https://help.shopify.com//manual/products/inventory/inventory-counts]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/fulfill-orders-in-batches; date: October 16, 2026; title: Fulfill orders in batches; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Shipping]; text: You can now fulfill orders together in batches. Group up to 250 fulfillments by criteria such as product type or shipping destination, then pick, buy labels, print documents, and pack them together. Each batch follows a workflow you can customize. By default it has three steps: * Pick: Print a pick list showing the products for every order in the batch. * Print: Buy shipping labels for all orders in the batch at once, then print packing slips, shipping labels, and customs forms together. * Pack: Scan to verify. A tone plays and a green checkmark appears for each correct item. A wrong or extra item plays an error tone and shows a red icon. Make the workflow your own: * Add, delete, or rename steps, and add actions to any step. * Drag steps and actions to reorder them. * Choose which documents print in each step. * Assign a staff member to each step. To get started, go to your Orders page, select the orders you want to fulfill, and click Create batch. You can also batch your most recent unfulfilled orders automatically. Learn more in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/fulfillment/fulfilling-orders/batch-fulfillment]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/buy-shipping-labels-on-shopify-now-in-the-netherlands-and-poland; date: October 16, 2026; title: Buy shipping labels on Shopify, now in the Netherlands and Poland; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Shipping]; text: Merchants who ship from the Netherlands or Poland can now buy DHL eCommerce shipping labels on Shopify. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/offer-royal-mail-pickup-points-at-checkout; date: October 15, 2026; title: Offer Royal Mail pickup points at checkout; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Royal Mail is now available as a pickup point provider across the UK. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/buy-shipping-labels-automatically-with-shopify-flow; date: October 15, 2026; title: Buy shipping labels automatically with Shopify Flow; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Shipping]; text: Merchants can now buy shipping labels with a Shopify Flow action. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/automatically-generated-policies-help-you-launch-faster; date: October 08, 2026; title: Automatically generated policies help you launch faster; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now automate your return and refund, contact information, terms of service, shipping, and legal notice policies to help you launch your store faster and expand into new markets. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/sidekick-skills; date: October 03, 2025; title: Save and share your best Sidekick prompts as skills; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Sidekick]; text: You can now save your most useful Sidekick prompts as custom skills and reuse them whenever you need them. Skills work well for tasks you do regularly, whether that's pulling specific reports, creating customer segments, writing content that matches your brand voice, or analyzing sales patterns. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-new-triggers-for-discounts-disputes-and-fulfillment-order-splits; date: October 02, 2025; title: Flow: New triggers for discounts, disputes, and fulfillment order splits; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Apps]; text: Four new triggers in Shopify Flow help you stay on top of your shop. You can now build workflows that respond when automatic discounts are created, discount codes are generated, Shopify Payments disputes are submitted, or fulfillment orders are split. Automated discount created starts a workflow when an automatic discount is created by you or by a third-party app in your store. Discount code created starts a workflow when a discount code is created by you or by a third-party app in your store. Dispute created starts a workflow when a chargeback or inquiry dispute is created for an order in your store that uses Shopify Payments. Fulfillment order split starts a workflow when a fulfillment order is split by you or by a third-party app and returns the original fulfillment order as well as fulfillment orders resulting from the split. These triggers give you instant visibility into promotional activity and payment issues, whether they're created by you or third-party apps. Use them to send Slack notifications when disputes arise, automatically tag orders that use specific discount types, or coordinate with fulfillment partners when orders are divided. Each trigger provides detailed data about the event, so you can create precise conditions and actions in your workflows. Find these new triggers in the Flow app under your Shopify admin, and start building automated responses to keep your operations running smoothly. For more information, visit the documentation. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/unit-pricing-is-now-available-globally; date: October 02, 2025; title: Unit pricing is now available globally; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Products]; text: You can now display how much products cost per unit of measurement, helping customers make informed purchasing decisions by showing: Price per weight (e.g. gram, ounce) Price per volume (e.g. liter, gallon) Price per length (e.g. meter, foot) Price per quantity (item count) For example: - $10.49/oz or $5.32/ft - $2.99 each Learn more about unit pricing.; links: [text: unit pricing; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/details/product-pricing/unit-pricing]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/pay-in-full-credit-card-payment-option-will-automatically-retry-each-month; date: October 01, 2025; title: Pay-in-Full credit card payment option will automatically retry each month; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Shopify Credit]; text: We’ve added automatic monthly retries to the Pay-in-full credit card payment option because this respects the merchants original choice. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/increased-shopify-credit-rewards-cap; date: October 01, 2025; title: Increased Shopify Credit rewards cap; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Shopify Credit]; text: Shopify Credit cardholders can now earn 3% cashback on their top spend category for up to $250,000 USD in eligible purchases each account year (up from $100,000 USD). After reaching $250,000 in your top spending category, you'll continue to earn 1% cashback on eligible purchases for the rest of your account year. You’ll still earn 1% cashback in all other rewardable spend categories. Learn more about Shopify Credit rewards and how cashback is calculated in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/finance/shopify-credit/rewards#calculating-your-cashback-rewards]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/merchants-can-now-dispute-balance-card-or-shopify-credit-card-transactions-in-their-account; date: October 01, 2025; title: Merchants can now dispute Balance card or Shopify credit card transactions in their account; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Shopify Credit]; text: Previously, you could only submit disputes for fraudulent transactions in your Shopify account. For other dispute reasons, you had to reach out to Shopify support. Now you can dispute for many reasons directly in your Shopify account. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/control-when-b2b-orders-require-review-at-checkout; date: October 01, 2025; title: Control when B2B orders require review at checkout; tags: [text: New]; areas: [B2B]; text: You can now dynamically determine which B2B orders require review using the Payment Customization Function. The new orderReviewAdd operation lets you define custom business rules to automatically send orders to draft for review based on conditions like order value, cart contents, or customer attributes. Use the Payment Customization Function API to implement complex B2B workflows such as requiring review for high-value orders, pre-order items, or new customer orders - giving you granular control over order validation beyond the static all-or-nothing setting. This operation is only available for B2B purchases on stores with the Plus plan.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flexible-top-items-in-reports; date: September 30, 2025; title: Flexible top items in reports; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Analytics]; text: On September 30, we launched the ability to configure the number of items that can be displayed in reports within Analytics. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/ddu-orders-now-captures-sales-tax-for-registered-destinations; date: September 29, 2025; title: DDU orders now captures sales tax for registered destinations; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Admin]; text: Taxes will now be calculated for merchants using our Duties and Import Taxes calculator, in countries they configured to not collect duties and have a tax registration. Learn more about collecting Duties and Import Taxes.; links: [text: Learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/duties-and-import-taxes/charging-duties]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/customize-return-and-exchange-receipts-in-pos; date: September 29, 2025; title: Customize return and exchange receipts in POS; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Return and exchange receipts are now fully customizable in Shopify POS, giving you the same design control you have with sales receipts. Use our Liquid template editor or visual editor to create professional, branded receipts for every transaction type. Access the feature through Settings > POS Channel > Settings > Receipts. Customize layouts to highlight important information, add return policies or promotional messaging, and include branded elements like logos and social media handles. With this update, you can now deliver a consistent, professional experience across all customer interactions, from initial sales through returns and exchanges. Learn more about return and exchange receipt customization.; links: [text: return and exchange receipt customization; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/shopify-pos/customize-pos/printed-receipts]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-email-now-supports-dynamic-product-sections; date: September 25, 2025; title: Shopify Email now supports dynamic product sections; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Shopify Email now supports dynamic product sections in your email campaigns and automations. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/phasing-out-support-for-sell-from-all-locations-fulfillable-inventory-setting; date: September 25, 2025; title: Products can no longer be sold outside of configured shipping zones; tags: [text: Removed]; areas: [Admin]; text: The "Sell from all locations to all shipping zones" option of fulfillable inventory is being removed. All shops will use the "Sell only within configured shipping zones" option. This change helps prevent overselling and reduces situations such as canceled orders due to stock unavailability for their region, or manual intervention to correct orders. What this means: At checkout, customers can only complete purchases for products that are in stock at a fulfillment location that is configured to deliver to their shipping zone. If an item is unavailable at all locations for the customer's shipping zone, then they can't purchase that item at checkout and will see delivery or stock related errors. This behaviour has already been enabled automatically for most shops. If your store hasn't been migrated yet, we've notified you directly and the change takes effect on September 30th. Learn more about fulfillable inventory and how to prepare for the change.; links: [text: Learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/fulfillment/setup/fulfillable-inventory]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-metafield-definition-types-article_reference-list-article_reference; date: September 23, 2025; title: New metafield definition types - article_reference / list.article_reference; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: As of API 2025-10, two new metafield types are available article_reference: A reference to an article on the online store. list.article_reference: A list of article references on the online store.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/segment-customers-based-on-the-product-categories-they-ve-browsed-or-bought; date: September 19, 2025; title: Segment customers based on the product categories they’ve browsed or bought; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Customers]; text: You can now group customers by the types of products they've viewed or purchased, making it easier to send relevant promotions and recommendations. The segmentation automatically includes customers in parent categories—so someone who bought "Facial Cleansers" will also appear in "Beauty" and "Health & Beauty" segments. This new filtering works with over 16,000 defined product categories from Shopify's standard product taxonomy and integrates directly with your existing segmentation workflow. Use these segments with Shopify Email, targeted discounts, or any marketing tool that supports customer segments. Start creating more targeted campaigns by exploring the new taxonomy filters in your customer segmentation tools. Learn more about customer segmentation in the Help Center.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-secure-your-workflows-with-with-liquid-filters-for-hashing-sha1-sha256-md5; date: September 12, 2025; title: Flow: Secure your workflows with with Liquid filters for hashing (sha1, sha256, md5); tags: [text: New]; areas: [Apps]; text: When connecting Flow to external APIs, you often need to hash API keys, customer data, or other sensitive information for security. You can now hash data directly in your Flow workflows using the same hashing functions in Liquid that Shopify themes uses, including: sha1, sha256, md5, hmac_sha1, and hmac_sha256. Simply add the filter to any variable in your workflow. For hmac filters, include an authentication code as a parameter. Examples: * Hash a customer email: {{ customer.defaultEmailAddress | sha1 }} * Hash a customer email using hmac_sha256: {{ customer.defaultEmailAddress | hmac_sha256: "your-secret-key" }} For complete filter documentation, check the Liquid reference for each filter. Questions? Visit the Shopify Community.; links: [text: Liquid reference; href: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/liquid/filters/hmac_sha256 | text: Shopify Community; href: https://community.shopify.com/c/shopify-flow/304]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/create-native-exchanges-for-facebook-meta-orders; date: September 12, 2025; title: Create native exchanges for Facebook (Meta) orders; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: Previously, when customers wanted to exchange items from Facebook orders, you had to: - Process a return on the original order - Create a new order for the exchange items For Facebook orders created as of August 26, 2025, you can now seamlessly create, track and manage exchanges for Facebook orders from your Shopify admin all within the same order, helping you maximize revenue retention. Offer exchanges across your entire product catalog and easily track and report on fees associated with returns, providing flexibility during the returns experience. Additionally, return fees could previously not be charged on a return, but are now available as well. Learn more about exchanges in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders/returns/creating-returns]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/flow-override-the-default-resource-used-by-actions; date: September 11, 2025; title: Flow: Override the default resource used by actions; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Apps]; text: Many Flow actions require a resource ID. For example, to update the product status, you need the product ID and the new status. By default, Flow analyzes your workflow and provides the product ID so that you don’t have to figure it out. When the workflow contains more than one resource of the same type, or when a “Run code” step is used to generate an ID, Flow might not choose the correct ID. This improvement allows you to specify a resource to build the automation you need. On actions that require a resource, you’ll now have an option to enter a variable or a specific resource’s GID (such as “gid://shopify/Product/144848548” and not “144848548”). For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.; links: [text: Shopify community; href: https://community.shopify.com/tag/flow]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/multi-store-reporting-is-now-available-in-analytics; date: September 09, 2025; title: Multi-store reporting now available in analytics; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Analytics]; text: New multi-store reporting brings analytics across stores in your organization into a single, comprehensive view so you don’t have to manually switch between admins to piece together insights across your business. Get started with the new default multi-store section of your analytics dashboard, or create a custom section based on your most critical KPIs. Multi-store reporting is available for Plus organizations with multiple stores. Users within eligible organizations must have full organization analytics permissions to access. View your analytics or learn more about setup and user permissions in the Help Center.; links: [text: View your analytics; href: http://admin.shopify.com/analytics | text: learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/organization-settings/analytics]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/send-customers-an-email-notification-when-they-receive-store-credit; date: September 09, 2025; title: Send customers an email notification when they receive store credit; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: A new cutomer notification email is now available when issuing store credit. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/sidekick-fullscreen-mode; date: September 05, 2025; title: Sidekick fullscreen mode; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Sidekick]; text: We've added fullscreen mode to Sidekick, giving you more space to work with Shopify's AI commerce assistant. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/use-any-hid-barcode-scanner-with-shopify-pos; date: September 04, 2025; title: Use any HID barcode scanner with Shopify POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: Expand your hardware choices with HID (keyboard-mode) scanner support for Shopify POS. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/discovery-and-public-price-lists-available-globally; date: September 04, 2025; title: Discovery and public price lists available globally in Shopify Collective; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Collective]; text: Discovery and public price lists are now available globally in Shopify Collective. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/authorize-custom-crawlers-and-tools-with-new-crawler-access-keys; date: August 29, 2025; title: Authorize custom crawlers and tools with Web Bot Auth; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Online Store]; text: Shopify now leverages Web Bot Auth and HTTP message signatures to let you securely authorize your own crawlers, scripts, or tools to access your public Shopify online store. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/grab-buyers-attention-on-after-checkout-by-building-an-announcement-bar-extension; date: August 28, 2025; title: Get buyers' attention after checkout using an announcement bar extension; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Checkout]; text: We are excited to announce the release of support for building announcement bar extensions on the Thank You page and Customer Account pages, including the Order Status page, Order Index page, and Profile page. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/storefront-api-buyer-authentication-from-cart-to-checkout-now-supports-vaulted-cards-and-store-credit; date: August 28, 2025; title: Storefront API buyer authentication from cart to checkout now supports vaulted cards and store credit; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Custom storefronts]; text: Vaulted cards and store credit are now supported in Checkout for buyers who have been authenticated with the Storefront API such as on headless storefront flows or mobile apps. Append the customerAccessToken into the Buyer Identity object of the Storefront API Cart and buyers now have access to their vaulted cards or store credit if applicable. For security reasons and best practices, request the checkoutUrl when the buyer is ready to navigate to checkout, this can be re-requested if needed. This ensures secure authentication while maintaining a smooth payment experience.; links: [text: authenticated with the Storefront API; href: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/continuous-cart-authentication-to-checkout | text: Append the customerAccessToken; href: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/headless/building-with-the-storefront-api/cart/manage#step-6-authenticate-customer-for-logged-in-checkouts]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/canada-post-now-available-duties-pre-paid-to-the-us; date: August 28, 2025; title: Canada Post duties-pre-paid labels now available to the US; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Canada Post duties-pre-paid now available into the US Starting August 29, international postal shipments to the US must be sent as DDP (Delivered Duties Paid). What this means for your business: * Merchants that wish to continue shipping with Canada Post must pre-pay the duties rather than having their customers pay upon delivery. * Merchants must activate Shopify duties calculations in order to purchase duties pre-paid labels via Shopify Shipping * DDU Canada Post shipments to the US will no longer be accepted and will be blocked at label creation. Required actions before August 28, 2025: In order to continue utilizing Canada Post to ship from Canada to the US: * Navigate to Settings > Taxes > Duties and enable duty collection for the U.S. market. * Use the bulk editor to add HS codes and Country of Origin to all products. * Go to Markets, select the United States, and modify duties display settings to either display import taxes and duties as a line at checkout or include duties costs in product prices. If the latter, consider reviewing your US market pricing to account for these changes. * Review the US shipping zone to ensure your shipping rate set up reflects DDP carriers and collects enough from buyers to fulfill your shipping strategy * If you work with an external fulfillment partner in Canada, verify your fulfillment provider can generate Canada Post DDP labels. If they cannot, then consider purchasing labels on Shopify. If you don't make these changes, your Canada Post labels to the U.S. will be blocked starting August 28, 2025. Consider commercial carriers (DHL Express or Purolator via Shopify Shipping) as alternatives if you prefer to maintain DDU shipping. To learn more about shipping with Canada Post to the US, please visit the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Settings > Taxes > Duties; href: https://admin.shopify.com/settings/taxes/duties | text: Markets; href: https://admin.shopify.com/markets/ | text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/fulfilling-orders/shipping-labels/shipping-carriers/canada-post#usa-shipping]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/variant-level-package-assignment; date: August 26, 2025; title: Set default packages for product variants; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now set default package dimensions and weights for specific products or product variants. At checkout, if applicable, the selected package will be used to calculate shipping rates for single item orders. When creating shipping labels for those items, the package information automatically populates based on your preset defaults, eliminating manual data entry and speeding up label creation. This is particularly useful for products that consistently ship in the same packaging. You can assign different package defaults to different products or variants, and still override the defaults when needed for specific shipments. Configure product package defaults in your product settings, or learn more in the Help Center.; links: [text: Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/setup/packaging/setting-up-packages]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/analytics-last-n-days-presets-now-includes-today-s-data; date: August 26, 2025; title: Analytics "Last N Days" presets now includes today's data; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: The “Last 7/30/90/365 days" preset date ranges in the Analytics date picker now automatically include today’s data, giving merchants a real-time view of performance by default. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/update-to-discounts-csv-discount-class-column; date: August 26, 2025; title: Update to Discounts CSV "Discount Class" column; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: Update We've updated the "Discount Class" column in the discount CSV export to help merchants better understand when a discount may be applied across products, total order value, and shipping. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/track-your-stock-with-new-bin-name-column; date: August 25, 2025; title: Track your stock with new “Bin name” column; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Inventory]; text: What’s new The Inventory CSV now includes a “Bin name” column. Enter a bin name (for example 05-A-03 or Front-Aisle-01) for each variant–location row and re-import the file to save it. Bin names appear on Pick lists, helping staff walk the warehouse in the right order. Bulk update bin names using the Inventory Bulk Editor View bin names directly on the Inventory Index page Why you’ll love it Faster picking – pick lists are printed in bin order, so staff spend less time searching. No third-party spreadsheets – keep bin name data in Shopify where your inventory already lives. How to get started From the Admin, go to Products ▸ Inventory ▸ Export and choose the “Current inventory” template. Open the CSV and fill in the new Bin name column for each variant/location that you want to label. Alternatively, use Bulk Editor from the Admin to update Bin name for each variant/location Save the file and re-import it in Products ▸ Inventory ▸ Import. Print a Pick list (Orders ▸ Fulfillment ▸ Pick lists); you’ll see the bin names beside each line item. Good to know Each variant can have one bin per physical name for now. Inventory quantities are still tracked at the location level. Bin names are free-text – add leading zeros if you need them to sort correctly (for example 01, 02 … 10). Learn more about bins in the Shopify Help Center; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/inventory/getting-started-with-inventory/bin-locations]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/prevent-accidental-inventory-overwrites-with-improved-csv-workflow; date: August 25, 2025; title: Updates to Inventory CSV file Columns; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Inventory]; text: Update We've added a On hand (new) column to the inventory CSV and renamed On hand to On hand (current). This helps prevent merchants from accidentally overwriting current stock quantities with outdated data. Now merchants can safely update bin names and other product details by leaving the On hand (new) field blank, and their current inventory levels stay untouched. Important If you use automated tools, scripts, or external systems with your inventory CSV, you’ll need to update them before using this feature. Otherwise, your imports or workflows may break. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/automate-your-fraud-settings; date: August 22, 2025; title: Automate your fraud settings; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Payments]; text: Automate your fraud settings Merchants using Shopify Payments can now automate fraud prevention settings to match Shopify recommendations. Once automated, these settings update automatically as recommendations change. Turning on automated fraud prevention settings will: * Turn off declining charges that fail AVS postal code verification, as this functionality is already included in the new fraud model, which uses over 400 fraud signals for more precise fraud detection * Turn on declining charges that fail CVV verification Learn more about fraud prevention in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/fraud-prevention/index]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/translate-your-shopify-forms-into-multiple-languages; date: August 20, 2025; title: Translate your Shopify Forms into multiple languages; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Apps]; text: Shopify Forms now lets you translate your form content into multiple languages, making it easier to reach and convert customers in international markets. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/issue-refunds-to-store-credit-when-cancelling-an-order; date: August 19, 2025; title: Issue refunds to store credit when cancelling an order; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Issuing store credit refunds helps ensure that you keep cash flowing back into your business and improves customer retention. You can also choose whether you'd like to set an expiration date for the store credit. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/retail-markets-are-now-available; date: August 19, 2025; title: Retail markets are now available.; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [POS]; text: Take control of your retail pricing strategy with location-specific catalogs. You can now set different prices for the same products across your retail locations, giving you the flexibility to optimize for local markets, store performance, or customer demographics. Whether you're running premium locations in high-rent districts or value stores in different markets, you now have the tools to price strategically while maintaining unified inventory management. Location-specific catalogs also improve POS performance with faster sync times and better handling of bulk operations across all your retail locations. Retail markets are available for all retailers on Shopify with a POS Pro subscription, using POS version 10.3 or above. Learn more about Retail markets; links: [text: Retail markets; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/markets]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/support-for-dynamic-product-bundles-on-pos; date: August 18, 2025; title: Support for Dynamic Product Bundles on POS; tags: [text: New]; areas: [POS]; text: You can now build and support dynamic product bundles on Shopify POS using three new capabilities: cartTransform API support on POS The cartTransform function is now supported on POS, enabling you to expand, merge, or modify cart line items in response to user interactions. This unlocks more complex bundle logic and pricing strategies, like mix-and-match and optional add-ons. Manage line-item UI extension target A new extension target has been added to the cart’s manage line item screen, giving developers a dedicated surface to display and manage bundle components in POS. This ensures more intuitive in-store configuration and editing. Split line-item support POS now supports splitting a single line item into multiple lines at checkout. This is required for dynamic bundles that need to itemize individual components while preserving bundle logic. Together, these updates give app developers the tools to build high-quality, omnichannel bundling experiences — with clean cart behavior, accurate inventory tracking, and better in-store workflows.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/pickup-in-store-for-b2b; date: August 15, 2025; title: Pickup in-store for B2B; tags: [text: New]; areas: [B2B]; text: If you're using Shopify B2B, you can now offer pickup in-store as a delivery option to your wholesale customers. This gives customers the flexibility to collect their orders directly from store locations instead of paying for shipping. Once enrolled in early access, you can create pickup locations in your admin and enable pickup in store for those locations. B2B customers will then see local pickup as an option during checkout alongside standard shipping methods. If you operate a blended store that serves both B2B and DTC customers, pickup in-store will be available to all customers by default. You can use Checkout Blocks to control which pickup locations are visible to specific customer types. Contact Plus Support to enable pickup in store for B2B, or learn more in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/b2b/checkout-and-orders/shipping-methods#pickup-in-store]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/convert-your-analytics-to-any-currency-instantly; date: August 15, 2025; title: Convert your analytics to any currency instantly; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Analytics]; text: A currency picker is now available on your Analytics dashboard and in every report, letting you convert monetary values to any currency you choose. This is especially useful if you sell in multiple currencies or want to analyze your performance in a specific currency. The conversion uses historical exchange rates from the original transaction dates, ensuring accuracy in your reporting. Your store's currencies will appear at the top of the picker for easy access, but you can select from any supported currency. You'll find the currency picker at the top of your Analytics dashboard and individual reports. Simply select your preferred currency and your data will update automatically.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/b2b-checkout-now-supports-apple-pay; date: August 13, 2025; title: B2B Checkout now supports Apple Pay; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: By enabling Apple Pay as a payment option, your wholesale customers can conveniently pay for their orders and invoices without manually entering credit card details, and you can easily reconcile payments within the admin. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/discounts-on-fulfilled-items; date: August 13, 2025; title: Discounts on fulfilled items; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Admin]; text: You can now apply discounts to fulfilled items, whereas previously, discounts were limited to unfulfilled items. This enhancement allows merchants to effectively issue partial refunds through discounts, improving post-purchase attribution and eliminating the need for manual refunds in this process. Additionally, orders will now automatically unarchive for edits and re-archive after issuing a refund, removing the need for manual unarchiving and archiving when making changes to an order.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/organize-your-analytics-dashboard-with-custom-sections; date: August 11, 2025; title: Organize your Analytics dashboard with custom sections; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Analytics]; text: You can now create custom sections on your Analytics dashboard to better organize your metric cards. Group related metrics together such as separating sales data from marketing metrics to create a dashboard layout that works for your business. To get started, click "Customize" on your Analytics dashboard, then "Add section" to create a new section. Give it a name, add the metric cards you want, and save your changes. You can create as many sections as you need, reorder them by dragging and dropping, and collapse or expand sections to focus on what matters most. This enhanced organization makes it easier to find the insights you need and creates a more personalized analytics experience tailored to how you analyze your business.

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/faster-resolution-for-paypal-wallet-disputes; date: August 11, 2025; title: Faster resolution for PayPal Wallet disputes; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Payments]; text: We’ve launched two improvements to the PayPal Wallet dispute process to help you save time and protect your revenue. This change ensures the disputed amount is limited to the specific item's value, which can help lower your costs in the case of a loss. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/arrange-app-blocks-more-easily-in-checkout-and-customer-accounts; date: August 07, 2025; title: Arrange app blocks more easily in checkout and customer accounts editor; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Checkout]; text: We’ve updated the Sections tab in the Checkout and Accounts Editor, allowing you to arrange app blocks exactly as they appear to customers. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/order-editing-now-supports-orders-with-duties-and-import-taxes; date: August 07, 2025; title: Edit orders with duties and import taxes; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [International]; text: Editing orders lets you make adjustments to an order after it's placed, like adding or removing products. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/customer-eligibility-for-automatic-discounts; date: August 06, 2025; title: Customer eligibility for automatic discounts; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Discounts]; text: We’ve added a new eligibility section for automatic discounts. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/credit-limits-change-with-your-business; date: August 01, 2025; title: Credit limits change with your business; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Shopify Credit]; text: Shopify Credit will automatically review your credit limit every month instead of every six months. If your limit changes, you’ll get a notification at the beginning of your statement period, and the new limit will take effect right away. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-draft-order-tag-limit; date: August 01, 2025; title: New draft order tag limit; tags: [text: Changed]; areas: [Admin]; text: In your Shopify admin, a draft order now has a limit of 250 tags. This limit was added to improve the performance of your Shopify store, and applies whether a tag is created manually or automatically by an app. A saved draft order that already includes more than 250 tags keeps the existing tags, but no more tags can be added to that draft order until it has fewer than 250 tags. You can delete tags from the draft order details page. Learn more about managing draft orders in Shopify from the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: managing draft orders in Shopify; href: http://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders/create-orders]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/shopify-collective-available-in-36-additional-countries; date: July 31, 2025; title: Shopify Collective available in 36 additional countries; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Collective]; text: Shopify Collective is now accessible in 36 additional countries, through direct connections with brand partners in the same country or region. Shopify Collective works in two ways: As a retailer, you can connect with your existing brand partners to source complementary products to expand your catalog without the risk of upfront inventory. Sourced products integrate into your catalog, and customer orders are automatically processed and forwarded to the brand partner for fulfillment. Install the Shopify Collective app, or learn more in the Help Center. As a supplier, you can distribute your products through existing brand partners' stores, to drive more sales through new sales channels. Install the Shopify Collective: Supplier app or learn more in the Help Center. All order processing, payment coordination, and fulfillment management between brand partners is automated through the platform.; links: [text: 36 additional countries; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/shopify-collective/retailers/requirements-and-considerations?utm_source=dotcom&utm_medium=changelog&utm_campaign=phaseonerollout#requirements | text: Shopify Collective app; href: https://apps.shopify.com/collective?utm_source=dotcom&utm_medium=changelog&utm_campaign=phaseonerollout | text: learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/shopify-collective/retailers?utm_source=dotcom&utm_medium=changelog&utm_campaign=phaseonerollout | text: Shopify Collective: Supplier app; href: https://apps.shopify.com/collective-supplier?utm_source=dotcom&utm_medium=changelog&utm_campaign=phaseonerollout | text: learn more; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/shopify-collective/suppliers?utm_source=dotcom&utm_medium=changelog&utm_campaign=phaseonerollout]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/image-generation-now-available-in-file-picker; date: July 28, 2025; title: Image generation now available in file picker; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Sidekick]; text: Whether you need a new hero banner for your theme or a new logo for an upcoming email campaign, the file picker now offers image generation. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/control-marketing-consent-on-all-your-shopify-forms; date: July 28, 2025; title: Control marketing consent on all your Shopify Forms; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Marketing]; text: You can now create any type of form—contact requests, job applications, warranty registrations, wholesale inquiries—without forcing customers into marketing emails they didn't ask for. Learn more about setting up marketing consent for email and SMS within Shopify Forms.; links: [text: Learn more about setting up marketing consent; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/forms-app/settings/all-forms#form]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/ship-and-carryout-now-supports-shopify-tax; date: July 25, 2025; title: Ship and carryout now supports Shopify Tax; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [POS]; text: Now retail staff can let customers carry out some items and ship others in a single transaction using the ship and carryout workflow. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/bulk-csv-importing-for-inventory-transfers; date: July 24, 2025; title: Bulk CSV Importing for Inventory Transfers; tags: [text: Feature]; areas: [Inventory]; text: You can now create inventory transfers by uploading a CSV file with product variants and quantities. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/new-theme-code-editor; date: July 22, 2025; title: New theme code editor; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Online Store]; text: We're rolling out a new theme code editor that brings powerful editing capabilities directly to your Shopify admin. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/refund-to-store-credit-when-processing-a-return; date: July 18, 2025; title: Issue refunds to store credit when processing a return or exchange; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Admin]; text: Issuing store credit refunds for a return or exchange helps ensure that you keep cash flowing back into your business and improves customer retention. Store credit can now be issued as a refund when you are processing a return. In the "Refund now" section, select "store credit" as the refund method. You also have the option to refund the order to a combination of original payment methods and store credit. In addition, you can choose whether you'd like to set an expiration date for the store credit. To refund orders to store credit, you must be the store owner or have the Refund to store credit order permission.; links: [text: Refund to store credit order permission; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/your-account/users/roles/permissions/store-permissions#orders-permissions]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/track-inventory-changes-with-new-adjustment-history-reports-model; date: July 18, 2025; title: Track inventory changes with new adjustment history reports & model; tags: [text: New]; areas: [Inventory]; text: A new set of inventory reports is now available in Analytics > Reports that provides comprehensive visibility into your inventory movements. These reports allow you to: Track every increase and decrease in inventory across all SKUs and locations View detailed history of inventory adjustments with timestamps and reasons for changes Monitor incoming shipment orders to see expected inventory arrivals by location Analyze transfer orders between locations Access complete audit trails for compliance requirements The reports provide historical data beyond the previous 180-day limit in Admin on a go-forward basis, allowing you to analyze long-term inventory trends and patterns. You can find these reports in the Analytics > Reports section of admin. Please note that you must be using new Shopify Analytics to view these reports. This enhancement helps answer critical questions like: Why did a specific SKU show negative inventory on a particular date? How much inventory is expected to arrive at each location? What transfer orders are pending between locations? Learn more about inventory reporting in the Shopify Help Center.; links: [text: new Shopify Analytics; href: https://help.shopify.com/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/new-analytics | text: Shopify Help Center; href: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/inventory/reports]

uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/image-alt-text-can-now-be-translated; date: July 17, 2025; title: Image ALT text can now be translated; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [International]; text: We've made an improvement that allows translation of image ALT text into different languages. uri: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/improved-theme-discovery-and-install-experience-on-the-shopify-theme-store; date: July 15, 2025; title: Improved theme discovery and install experience on the Shopify Theme Store; tags: [text: Improvement]; areas: [Themes]; text: We’ve shipped improvements to the Shopify Theme Store that make it easier than ever to find the perfect theme for your business—and get launched faster. Whether you’re selling sneakers or skincare, you’ll find options designed to convert in your category. Smarter filters by industry and catalog size We’ve improved how you browse and search with new filters that help you narrow in on exactly what you need. Faster launches with pre-configured theme files When you install a theme, the template you start with comes pre-configured with the same content and features in the demo store, helping you launch your website faster with less setup required.
